_about: Plain-English notes for the Studio Guide's Model directory, keyed by model id. Researched Oct 2026 from the makers' docs, Segmind's write-ups, independent reviews and our own runs. Specs (price, lengths, sizes) are NOT written here: the guide builds them live.

gpt-image-2.5-sunburst.summary: OpenAI's most careful image model, the precision half of GPT Image 2.5 (September 2026). It writes a picture from words, or edits the pictures you attach and leaves everything else alone. For finished campaign, packaging and poster frames.
good: Writes words in the picture cleanly, including track lists, small print and non-Latin scripts.
Edits only what you name: swap a label, a product or a line of copy and the jar, shelf and light stay put.
Keeps an attached product or person recognisable when you move them into a new scene.
Holds a person and their clothes together over repeated edits better than GPT Image 2 did.
Can return a cut-out on a transparent background for logos, stickers and product drops.
limits: Slower than its sibling Flare for the same job; OpenAI pitches it for precision, not volume.
Edits can still drift: a background swap may lose a product label, so check fine details.
No seed, so you can't repeat a result exactly.
gpt-image-2.5-sunburst.best_for: Final product, packaging and poster frames where the words must read
gpt-image-2.5-sunburst.tip: Find the picture in Flare, then switch to Sunburst for the final pass or a fussy edit. Put any wording in quotes, name the one thing to change and say 'keep everything else the same'.

nano-banana-2.1.summary: Google's newest everyday Nano Banana (the image side of Gemini), released in October 2026 as the update to Nano Banana 2. Writes pictures from words or edits and blends up to 14 reference pictures, with strong text and layout.
good: Clean text and layout: labelled diagrams, menus, posters and infographics come out spelled right.
Blends several reference pictures into one scene and keeps up to four people and ten objects recognisable.
Plain-language edits change the named thing and leave the table, background and light alone.
Very wide and very tall frames for banners and panoramas, without the repeated-tile look of earlier versions.
Has a seed, so you can repeat a take.
limits: Google's own notes still flag blurry small text and left/right mix-ups.
A notch below Nano Banana Pro on the densest, most detailed briefs.
Can't make transparent cut-outs.
nano-banana-2.1.best_for: Everyday keyframes, product mockups and pictures with labels or layout
nano-banana-2.1.tip: Refer to attachments by position ('the first reference picture', 'the second') and say what must stay. Its own default size is small: pick a larger one for finals.

seedream-5-pro.summary: ByteDance's top still-image model. It makes a picture from words, or edits a picture you attach and changes only the part you describe. It's strongest on words inside the picture and on busy layouts like posters and infographics.
good: Writes legible text inside the picture, in many languages: menus, labels, headlines, signs. Put the exact words in quotes.
Edits one thing and leaves the rest alone: recolour a product, swap a material, replace an object, with the lighting kept.
Takes a full set of reference pictures, so it can hold a product or person, or combine several pictures into one scene.
Lays out dense information well: posters, timelines, simple charts, mock app screens.
In side-by-side tests its photoreal pictures hold their own against the other top image models, with natural skin and materials.
limits: Doesn't go as large as Seedream 4.5 or 4.0, so big prints need an upscale afterwards.
One of the slower still models here; not the one for rapid-fire drafts.
Very small text can still waver. Proofread every word before anything ships.
No seed, so you can't rerun the exact same picture.
seedream-5-pro.best_for: Product edits and layouts where the words in the picture must be right
seedream-5-pro.tip: To edit, attach the picture and describe only the change, e.g. 'make the mug cobalt blue, keep everything else'. If there are two similar objects, say where the one you mean sits in the frame.

flux-3.summary: Black Forest Labs' newest still-image model (2026). It makes a picture from words, or edits and combines up to ten reference pictures when you attach them. Strongest on exact layout, legible text and large print-ready files.
good: Puts named items exactly where you want them: you can pin each element to a box on the frame instead of hoping it reads your layout.
Writes legible signs, labels and headlines, including non-Latin scripts such as Hindi (Devanagari).
Edit mode changes only what you name (recolour a product, move or remove an object) and leaves the rest of the photo untouched.
Can look things up on the web first, so a named landmark or real product comes out true to life.
Renders large print-size files directly, so fine texture and small type hold up when cropped.
limits: One of the slower stills here, so it's poor for rapid trial and error; FLUX 3 Klein does the same tricks faster.
No seed in the Studio, so you can't re-run the exact same picture with one small change.
Box layouts mean typing coordinates into the prompt, which is fiddly by hand.
Still new: BFL's quality claims come from its own tests, with little independent checking yet.
flux-3.best_for: Layouts, packaging and print pictures where placement and text must be right
flux-3.tip: With several reference pictures, call them Image 1, Image 2 in the prompt and say which gives the product and which the scene. For edits, end with 'keep everything else exactly unchanged'.

nano-banana-pro.summary: Google's top-tier Nano Banana (Gemini 3 Pro Image, late 2025). It thinks a brief through before drawing, so it handles dense, many-part briefs, accurate text in many languages, and up to 14 reference pictures.
good: Accurate, legible text in many languages: posters, infographics, packaging, UI mockups.
Handles complex briefs and detailed diagrams that cheaper models garble.
Mixes many reference pictures and keeps subject and style consistent across a series.
Has a seed for repeatable takes.
limits: Slower than Nano Banana 2.1 because it reasons first, and one of the dearer image models here.
Tends to over-polish: ask for grainy CCTV or a scrappy zine look and you get a clean version of it.
Can't make transparent cut-outs.
nano-banana-pro.best_for: Hard briefs: dense layouts, multilingual text, many-reference composites
nano-banana-pro.tip: Its own default is the largest, priciest size. Draft small, then re-run the keeper at full size.

gpt-image-2.5-flare.summary: OpenAI's everyday GPT Image 2.5 model, the fast half of the family. Same skills as Sunburst (readable text, careful edits from attached pictures, transparent cut-outs) with quicker turnaround, so it suits trying many directions.
good: Quick for this quality, so you can explore several ideas in one sitting.
Spells words correctly on labels, signs and posters, including small print on curved packaging.
Attach a picture and it edits just what you ask, e.g. recolour a scooter while chrome, plate and shadow stay.
Transparent-background output for logos, stickers and product cut-outs.
OpenAI's recommended default for most image work.
limits: Less careful than Sunburst on fussy edits; if it keeps disturbing parts you asked to keep, move up.
No seed, so a good result can't be repeated exactly.
Small details like labels can still slip after a background edit; check each pass.
gpt-image-2.5-flare.best_for: Fast drafts and everyday stills with readable text
gpt-image-2.5-flare.tip: A good keyframe model for the Board: quick, and it keeps a kit product recognisable when you attach it as a reference picture.

flux-2-max.summary: The top tier of Black Forest Labs' FLUX.2 line (late 2025). 'Max' bought you BFL's best prompt-following and most consistent editing in that generation, plus a web lookup for real things. Now overtaken by FLUX 3.
good: Follows long, many-part prompts closely; BFL says it beats FLUX.2 Pro on every measure.
Keeps a person, product or style consistent from up to ten reference pictures.
Can draw on current web information, so real products and places render accurately.
Convincing photoreal light and materials; good at retexturing a surface while keeping its shape.
Takes a seed, so you can repeat a result exactly and tweak one thing at a time.
limits: Superseded by FLUX 3, which adds box layout control and bigger files.
One of the pricier stills here.
Smaller largest size than FLUX 3, so less room to crop for print.
flux-2-max.best_for: Photoreal product and people shots that must match reference pictures
flux-2-max.tip: Once you like a picture, lock the seed and change one word at a time to steer it.

grok-imagine-image-2.summary: xAI's second-generation image model, the one behind Grok's Quality mode. Writes pictures from words or edits up to three attached pictures, and plans type and layout like a designer.
good: Plans text and layout before drawing, so headlines, labels and posters come out readable.
Edits are scoped: change one thing and the subjects you supplied stay as they were.
Combine a subject, a style and a scene from separate reference pictures in one go.
Lots of tall and wide frame shapes for phone screens and banners.
limits: Reviewers still found errors in long paragraphs and complex typography.
Takes three reference pictures, and its top size is smaller than the GPT and Nano Banana flagships.
When you attach a picture, that picture's shape sets the frame; your shape choice is ignored.
No seed.
grok-imagine-image-2.best_for: Posters, social graphics and scoped edits with readable text
grok-imagine-image-2.tip: Write it like a design brief: subject, layout, the exact words in quotes and where they sit, then style and light. Say what each reference picture is for.

wan2.7-image-pro.summary: The top tier of Alibaba's Wan 2.7 picture model. It plans the layout before it draws, so long, detailed prompts land where you asked, and it makes files big enough for print. It writes clean text in about a dozen languages.
good: Follows long, many-part prompts: in a reviewer's poster test it was one of only two models to put the chalkboard where the prompt said.
Clean, well-spaced lettering on signs, labels and packaging, in many languages.
Makes the largest pictures in the Alibaba line, enough to print or to crop several assets from one frame.
Edits too: attach a reference picture and describe the change.
Takes exact brand colours written into the prompt.
limits: Takes one reference picture here, so it can't hold a whole kit of people and products at once.
With a reference picture attached it can't make its largest size; edits come out smaller.
Slower and dearer than standard Wan 2.7 Image; more than you need for drafts.
Independent testing is thin so far; most praise comes from Alibaba and resellers.
wan2.7-image-pro.best_for: Print-size layouts where text must read and things must sit where you put them
wan2.7-image-pro.tip: Spell out positions plainly ('red chair front left, window behind, headline across the top') and put exact wording in quotes. Draft on standard Wan 2.7 Image first.

kling-3-image.summary: Kling's current still-image model. It writes a picture from words, or reworks a picture you attach. Aimed at photoreal people, products and lifestyle scenes, and a good source of Board keyframes.
good: Photoreal people, products and interiors with believable light and materials
Strong composition from a plain description; understands lens, angle and lighting words
Holds a person's likeness well when you rework or restage a reference picture
Takes a 'things to avoid' list to keep out clutter, blur or stray text
limits: Not for words in the picture: short labels sometimes work, longer copy comes out garbled or in mixed fonts
Edits can skip part of an instruction, so check the result against what you asked for
The Studio sends one reference picture, so it can't combine a person, a product and a place in one go
Slower than most still-image models here
kling-3-image.best_for: Photoreal lifestyle and product stills, and Board keyframes
kling-3-image.tip: Add prices, slogans and logos afterwards in a layout tool rather than asking the model to write them.

ideogram-4.5.summary: Ideogram's newest model (autumn 2026). Ideogram is the typography specialist: quote the words and it spells them right in posters, logos, packaging and signs. In the Studio it makes pictures from words only.
good: Spells quoted words correctly across several lines, weights and fonts in one picture.
Handles other languages and accents (umlauts, diacritics) when you name the language.
Lays out headline, sub-copy and artwork like a designer would: gig posters, menus, labels, infographics.
Quick for its quality, and big enough that dense small print stays crisp.
limits: No reference pictures here, so it can't keep your product, person or brand style. Ideogram's 4.5 editing mode isn't offered in the Studio.
Long or unusual words, prices and numbers can still slip; check every character before it ships.
Photoreal faces are Ideogram's weak spot; pick it for text and design, not portraits.
ideogram-4.5.best_for: Posters, labels, signs and logos where every word must be spelled right
ideogram-4.5.tip: Put each exact phrase in quotes and keep it short. Name the look ('two-colour risograph', 'flat vector') and the language if it isn't English.

recraft-v4-pro.summary: The high-resolution tier of Recraft V4, a design-first model built with professional designers. It makes finished-looking posters, packaging and product heroes with legible text, at print size.
good: Output looks art-directed: balanced layout and a cohesive palette even from a short prompt.
Renders short titles, taglines and labels as part of the layout, not pasted on top.
Large, print-ready files with convincing materials (steel, glass, fabric), so heroes hold up full-bleed.
Up to ten style pictures hold one look across a campaign set.
Ranges from photoreal close-ups to flat, stylized illustration.
limits: Its reference pictures copy a look (colour, technique, texture), not your actual product or person.
Keep text to two or three short blocks; long copy gets less reliable.
One of the priciest stills here; draft on plain Recraft V4 first.
recraft-v4-pro.best_for: Print-ready posters, packaging and box art with a designer's eye
recraft-v4-pro.tip: Draft on Recraft V4, then rerun the winning prompt here. Quote the words, and name materials and one light direction rather than stacking adjectives.

recraft-v4.summary: Recraft's standard V4 model: design-first pictures with legible text and a strong sense of layout and colour, at everyday web size. Cheap and quick, so a good first stop for ad and social graphics.
good: Treats type as part of the design, so titles, menus and packaging copy sit naturally in the layout.
Looks deliberate rather than stock: tidy composition and a cohesive palette.
Ranges from photoreal close-ups to flat, stylized illustration.
Up to ten style pictures keep a series in one look.
Inexpensive and quick, so you can try many layouts.
limits: Web-size output only; for print or big crops, use Recraft V4 Pro.
Style pictures copy a look, not a specific product or face.
Best with short to mid-length phrases; paragraphs of copy break down.
recraft-v4.best_for: Social and ad graphics with a headline, drafted fast
recraft-v4.tip: Quote the exact words and keep the title short. For a series, attach the same one or two style pictures to every run.

qwen-image-2.1-pro.summary: The Pro tier of Qwen Image 2.1, Alibaba's newest open picture model. One model both makes and edits pictures, takes up to ten reference pictures, sets type well, and can hand back a real see-through background.
good: Can return a truly transparent background, so stickers, icons and product cut-outs need no separate background removal.
Takes up to ten reference pictures: dress a person in a garment from another photo, or put a product in a scene, keeping both recognisable.
Strong type and layout for posters, packaging and infographics, in English and Chinese.
Edits by instruction: recolour an object, swap a background, add or remove things, or lift a subject out of a photo.
limits: Spelling is good but not perfect; proof every line of copy.
Transparency isn't guaranteed: name a backdrop, or let its prompt rewriter run, and you can get a painted checkerboard. Check the file.
Web-sized files; not the pick for large prints.
qwen-image-2.1-pro.best_for: Type-led layouts, and logos, stickers or cut-outs on a transparent background
qwen-image-2.1-pro.tip: For a see-through background, write 'transparent background, real alpha channel, no background fill' and describe no backdrop. Refer to references as 'the first image', 'the second image'.

p-image-ideogram.summary: Pruna's fast version of an Ideogram text-to-image model, made together with Ideogram. It's for pictures where words must read: posters, ads, packaging, thumbnails. You give it words only; it takes no reference pictures.
good: Spells short headlines and labels correctly far more often than other fast models
Photoreal people, products, food and interiors hold up well for a fast model
Quick and cheap enough to try many layouts before you commit
Has a 2K setting that keeps small lettering crisp
limits: Long text breaks down: single words or 2 to 4 word phrases come out most reliably
Heavily stylised or illustrated looks are weaker than its photo and lettering work (its maker says so)
The Studio runs it at its top quality setting, which can add detail you didn't ask for when the prompt is vague
No reference pictures, so it can't keep a real product or person from a photo
p-image-ideogram.best_for: Fast posters, ad mock-ups and packaging where a short headline must read
p-image-ideogram.tip: Put the exact words in quotes and keep them short. Choose 2K when the lettering is small or the piece is final.

flux-3-klein.summary: The small, fast, low-cost member of FLUX 3 ('Klein' is German for small). It has the same tricks as FLUX 3 (box layout, legible text, edits from up to ten pictures) for a fraction of the cost and wait.
good: One of the cheapest and quickest good-quality stills here, so you can try many takes.
Same box-layout control as FLUX 3: pin each item to a spot on the frame.
Legible signs and labels, including non-Latin scripts.
Edit mode recolours, swaps or moves one thing and keeps the rest of the photo as it was.
Has a seed, so you can repeat a picture and change one thing.
limits: Smaller than the full FLUX 3, so FLUX 3 is the safer pick for a hero image.
No web lookup, so real landmarks and products may come out generic.
The largest size is much slower than the rest; keep it for finals.
flux-3-klein.best_for: Fast, cheap drafts and Board keyframes with real layout control
flux-3-klein.tip: Find the composition here, then rerun the same prompt on FLUX 3 for the final. In edits, put the picture being changed first and list what must stay.

qwen-image-2.1-turbo.summary: The quick, low-cost tier of Qwen Image 2.1. It has the same features as Pro (making and editing, ten reference pictures, transparent backgrounds, good type) on a shorter run, making it one of the cheapest ways to try ideas here.
good: One of the cheapest and quickest picture models in the Studio, yet it still edits and combines pictures.
Real transparent backgrounds for cut-outs, stickers and logos.
Ten reference pictures for try-ons, product-in-scene shots and recolours that keep shape, texture and branding.
Readable English and Chinese text with sensible layout.
limits: A prompt that mentions any background can come back opaque even when you asked for transparency; check the file.
Long or tiny text can slip; proofread before use.
Web-sized files; not for large prints.
qwen-image-2.1-turbo.best_for: Fast, cheap drafts, cut-outs and quick product recolours
qwen-image-2.1-turbo.tip: Find the idea here, then rerun the winning prompt on Qwen Image 2.1 Pro for the final.

seedream-v5-lite.summary: The cheaper, quicker version of Seedream 5. 'Lite' means a lower price and a shorter wait, with some polish given up. It makes pictures from words, and switches to editing when you attach pictures.
good: Follows long, specific instructions closely: who is where, what they're doing, which style.
Good at text and layout for the price: titles, infographics, two-language signs.
Attach pictures and it edits them: restyle, relight, change the background, or merge several into one.
Takes more reference pictures than any other Seedream here, which helps with mood-board style blends.
Goes larger than Seedream 5.0 Pro.
limits: Reviewers find its pictures can look more obviously AI-made than Seedream 4.5's.
People occasionally come out oddly proportioned. Seedream 4.5 is steadier for portraits and products.
Tiny, dense text is less crisp than on Seedream 4.5 or 5.0 Pro.
No seed, so a good result can't be repeated exactly.
seedream-v5-lite.best_for: Cheap drafts, text-heavy graphics, and quick edits of an attached picture
seedream-v5-lite.tip: When editing, say what to keep as well as what to change: 'keep the composition and the face, change the jacket to red'. It holds the rest better when you tell it to.

z-image-turbo.summary: A small, very fast open picture model from Alibaba's Tongyi lab. It makes good-looking photoreal pictures, with some English and Chinese text, for very little. A sketchpad for ideas rather than a finisher.
good: Among the fastest and cheapest picture models here, so you can try many ideas quickly.
Photoreal results that look better than its speed suggests.
Better-than-average lettering for a small model, in English and Chinese.
Follows plain, direct prompts well.
limits: Little variety: a new seed often gives nearly the same composition.
Groups of people can come out sharing the same face.
Busy scenes with many subjects are weaker than on the big flagships.
No reference pictures, so it can't edit or keep a person consistent.
z-image-turbo.best_for: Quick photoreal drafts and mood frames when speed matters
z-image-turbo.tip: If your takes look alike, change the wording (angle, setting, light) rather than just the seed.

p-image.summary: Pruna's cheapest, fastest text-to-image model. Use it for quick drafts, mood boards and trying out ideas, not for final hero pictures.
good: One of the cheapest and quickest pictures in the Studio
Works well from short, plain descriptions; it fills in the detail itself
Covers a wide range of styles, from photo to illustration
Repeatable results when you keep the same seed
limits: Small pictures only, about 1,000 pixels on the long side, so upscale anything you keep for print
Not reliable for words inside the picture; use P Image (Ideogram) for that
Struggles with long, complicated prompts that have many parts
Less detail and polish than the big flagship models
p-image.best_for: Cheap first drafts and mood boards
p-image.tip: Keep the prompt short and concrete. When a draft works, rerun the idea on a flagship model or upscale the keeper.

hidream-l1-fast.summary: The fast version of HiDream-I1, an open-source image model from 2025 (MIT licence). Cheap, quick pictures from words, good for rough ideas and volume.
good: One of the cheapest and quickest stills here, so throwaway ideas cost almost nothing.
Follows prompts well for an open model, across photo, illustration and concept-art styles.
Can manage a short line of text, like a word or two on a sign.
limits: Takes no reference pictures, so it can't hold a product or a face from a photo.
The fast version trades detail for speed; clearly behind current flagships on realism and text.
Smaller top size than the flagships.
hidream-l1-fast.best_for: Cheap, quick rough ideas and mood frames

flux-kontext-max.summary: The top tier of FLUX.1 Kontext (mid-2025), Black Forest Labs' first model that edits a picture from a plain instruction. 'Max' was Kontext's best tier for following instructions and drawing type. Works from words alone too.
good: Edits from a plain sentence: 'make it night', 'change the jacket to red', 'remove the sign'.
Keeps a face or product recognisable across a few edits in a row.
Better at type than Kontext Pro: can add or change words on a sign or package.
Quick and moderately priced.
limits: Takes only one reference picture.
Older generation: FLUX 3 makes the same kind of edit with more control and up to ten pictures.
Picture quality can drift after many edits in a row; go back to the original if it turns soft.
flux-kontext-max.best_for: Quick one-picture edits from a plain instruction
flux-kontext-max.tip: Say what to change and what to keep, e.g. 'change the car to blue, keep the background and lighting the same'.

gpt-image-1.5.summary: OpenAI's late-2025 image model. Writes from words, or switches to its edit version when you attach reference pictures. Known for edits that keep faces and logos intact. Since overtaken by GPT Image 2 and 2.5.
good: Edits change the thing you name while keeping faces, logos and lighting intact.
Better text than GPT Image 1, including denser and smaller copy.
Photoreal light and materials; also handles charts and diagrams.
Can return transparent backgrounds for cut-outs.
limits: Only three frame shapes (square, landscape, portrait) and a modest top size.
Dearer than GPT Image 2.5, which does the same jobs at least as well.
Busy scenes with overlapping elements can still show glitches after an edit.
No seed.
gpt-image-1.5.best_for: Careful edits to a photo that must keep a face or logo exact
gpt-image-1.5.tip: Attach the photo, say what changes and what stays. For new work, try GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst first.

seedream-4.5.summary: The previous Seedream and still a strong all-rounder. It makes photoreal pictures from words and works well with reference pictures, keeping a face or product steady across a set. It goes larger than Seedream 5.
good: Photoreal light, shadow and reflections. A dependable choice for product and lifestyle shots.
Keeps a person or product looking the same across several pictures when you attach references.
Edits an attached picture from a plain instruction: change the background, the outfit, the season.
Produces large files, up to print size, larger than Seedream 5 can.
Short text in the picture, such as headlines and labels, usually comes out readable.
limits: An independent benchmark rated it lower on repeatability: the same request can come back quite different.
For dense text, or editing one small area precisely, Seedream 5.0 Pro does better.
At its largest size, wide or tall shapes come out with fewer pixels than a square does.
No seed, so you can't rerun an exact picture.
seedream-4.5.best_for: Photoreal product and lifestyle stills, and keeping a face across a set
seedream-4.5.tip: When editing, set the shape to match your original picture. A different shape makes it recompose or crop the scene.

qwen-image-edit-plus.summary: Alibaba's autumn-2025 Qwen editor (version 2509). Give it one to three pictures and an instruction and it changes what you ask, keeping faces, products and text. Quick and cheap, but Qwen Image 2.1 has since overtaken it.
good: Combines up to three pictures, such as a person, a product and a setting, keeping faces and product details recognisable.
Edits text inside a picture and keeps the font and colour.
Reads depth, edges and pose from your picture, so the layout of the scene holds through the edit.
Quick and cheap for an editor; fine for lots of small fixes.
limits: Three pictures at most, against ten for Qwen Image 2.1.
Older generation: Qwen Image 2.1 does the same jobs and adds transparent backgrounds.
It doesn't keep your photo's shape by itself; a different shape setting reframes the edit.
qwen-image-edit-plus.best_for: Quick multi-picture edits, like putting this product in that person's hand
qwen-image-edit-plus.tip: Set the shape to match your source photo, and name what must not change ('keep her face and the label exactly').

p-image-edit.summary: Pruna's fast, cheap picture editor. Attach one or more reference pictures and describe the change: restyle it, swap something, or combine several pictures into one.
good: Quick, low-cost edits from plain instructions
Can combine pictures, e.g. put the product from one into the scene of another
Can keep the shape of your original picture
Good for trying many edit ideas before paying for a pricier editor
limits: Its maker documents up to five reference pictures per edit, although the Studio lets you attach more
Weaker on complex, many-step instructions; keep each run to one clear change
Words inside the picture are unreliable
Less fine detail than the flagship editors
p-image-edit.best_for: Quick, cheap edits and simple composites
p-image-edit.tip: Say how the pictures should combine, e.g. 'put the bottle from picture 2 on the table in picture 1'. One change per run works best.

bria-expand-image.summary: Bria's outpainting tool: it extends the picture past its edges to a new shape and invents the extra scenery. Bria trains only on licensed images, which makes it a safer pick for pictures we license.
good: Turns an upright shot into a wide banner, or the reverse, without cropping the subject
The new areas usually match the light and texture of the original
Trained on licensed images only, which matters for commercial use
An optional prompt and 'things to avoid' steer what fills the new space
limits: The added area is invented: never use it where the real surroundings matter (news, documentary, real places)
It grows the picture evenly around the original; you can't choose one side in the Studio
Choosing the same shape as the original leaves nothing to add
The further it reaches from the original, the more generic the fill gets
bria-expand-image.best_for: Changing a picture's shape for a layout without cropping
bria-expand-image.tip: Pick a shape clearly different from the original. A short prompt for the new area ('more sandy beach') helps; leave it blank to just continue the scene.

veo-3.1.summary: Google's flagship video model. Makes short clips with sound from words or a start frame, can land on an end frame, and takes up to four reference pictures to keep a product, character or look consistent.
good: Sound comes with the picture: ambience, effects, music and spoken lines with mouths that match.
Ambient sound is a particular strength; reviewers rate it among the best.
Start frame plus end frame makes it a strong Board animator for planned transitions.
Reference pictures keep a product, character or look consistent across takes.
Responds well to film language: camera moves, lenses, light.
limits: Refuses real people: it won't work from a real person's photo or likeness. The Studio marks it 'no real people'.
Short clips only, landscape or vertical only.
With reference pictures attached, Google only makes 8-second clips.
In tests, sound effects sometimes landed late and cause and effect got missed.
veo-3.1.best_for: Polished hero shots with sound; Board shots that must hit a start and end frame
veo-3.1.tip: Write the shot beat by beat: action, camera move, ambience, and any spoken line in quotes. Turn sound off if you'll score it yourself.

kling-3-pro.summary: Kling 3.0 in its Pro tier: the same model as Standard, given more effort for tighter motion and detail. Writes a clip from words, or animates a still you attach, with sound made in the same pass. Kling's prompt-first flagship for finished shots.
good: Natural body motion: walking, gestures, hair and fabric move convincingly
Makes sound with the picture: ambience, effects and short lines of speech
With a still attached it can also land on an end frame, so a Board shot hits both keyframes
Follows shot-list prompts and camera directions such as dolly in, wide shot or handheld
Takes a 'things to avoid' list
limits: Speech is made in English or Chinese only
No reference pictures here, so it can't keep a kit person or product exact across shots
From words alone there's no end frame; the end frame only works when you also give a start frame
Takes a few minutes per clip
kling-3-pro.best_for: Finished hero shots and Board takes that need natural motion and sound
kling-3-pro.tip: Write it like a shot list: subject, action, setting, then the camera move and the light. Name the sounds you want, and keep any spoken line short.

seedance-2.5.summary: ByteDance's newest video model, from mid-2026. It makes a clip with sound from words, a start frame or a big kit of reference pictures. It can hold one take for up to half a minute, with several shots inside one clip.
good: Long single takes with sound that stays in step: dialogue, effects, music and ambience made together with the picture.
Several shots in one clip: write 'Shot 1: … Shot 2: …' and it cuts roughly where you ask.
Takes a large kit of reference pictures to keep a character, product or palette the same through the clip.
Follows camera directions well. Testers found locked-off, orbit, dolly and handheld moves came out as written.
Start and end frames both work, for controlled transitions.
limits: Blocks photos of real people's faces as a start frame, so it can't animate a photo of a real person.
Slow and unpredictable: several minutes a take, and the same request can take far longer one time than the next.
Its safety check runs on the finished clip, so a refusal can come after the full wait. Naming a film stock once triggered one.
Can't use a start frame and reference pictures together. An end frame only works with a start frame, so no Lead-in.
seedance-2.5.best_for: Finished ad spots and long takes with sound, from words or a kit
seedance-2.5.tip: Write the shot as it unfolds: subject and action, then setting, camera move, then the sound. Call kit pictures '@Image 1', '@Image 2' in the prompt and say what each one is for.

sora-2-pro.summary: OpenAI's higher-quality Sora 2 video model: clips with synced sound from words or a start frame. OpenAI retired the Sora 2 API on 24 September 2026 (its deprecations page confirms it), so runs are likely to fail.
good: Strong sense of physics and cause and effect: things fall, splash and collide believably.
Makes synced sound and dialogue with the picture.
Longer takes than most models here, and a sharper large size than plain Sora 2.
limits: Retired by OpenAI on 24 Sept 2026: expect runs to fail. Use Veo 3.1 instead.
Rejects start frames that show a human face, and refuses real people.
The start frame must match the clip's exact size and shape, or the take fails or distorts.
Slow, and no end frame, reference pictures or seed.
sora-2-pro.best_for: Physics-heavy shots with sound, if it still runs
sora-2-pro.tip: Try a short take first to see whether it still runs. If it fails, Veo 3.1 is the closest replacement with sound.

wan3.0-video.summary: Alibaba's newest video model (launched August 2026). One model writes clips from words, a start frame or reference pictures, makes the sound in the same pass, and runs single takes of up to 30 seconds.
good: Long single takes, up to half a minute, so a whole camera move or exchange plays out without cuts.
Makes a soundtrack with the picture: voices, ambience and effects, in several languages.
Takes a start frame, an end frame and reference pictures, so it suits Board keyframes and kit-based shots.
A reviewer rated its physics highly (breaking glass, colliding balls) and saw faces and outfits hold across long takes.
Lower cost per second than its faster Prime tier.
limits: Can cut to a camera angle nobody asked for; the most common complaint in testing.
Alibaba says sound texture and text inside the video still need work; check any signage.
Slow: several minutes a clip, longer for long takes.
With a start frame or reference attached, the shape comes from the picture, not your aspect setting.
wan3.0-video.best_for: Long single-take shots with sound; Board shots that start or end on a keyframe
wan3.0-video.tip: Write the sound you want into the prompt, and add 'one continuous shot, no cuts' to discourage surprise angle changes. Ask for at least 2 seconds.

flux-3-video.summary: Black Forest Labs' first video model, part of FLUX 3. It makes clips with sound (dialogue, effects, ambience) from words, or animates a start frame. Long single takes are possible.
good: Sound is made with the picture: speech with mouths that match, plus effects and room tone, in one pass.
Among the longest single clips here, so a whole beat can play out without stitching.
Wide style range, from live-action looks to animation and motion graphics.
Can start from a still, so it works for animating Board keyframes.
limits: One of the most expensive and slowest video models here: expect a long wait per clip.
In the Studio it takes a start frame only: no end frame and no kit reference pictures.
Long multi-shot clips still need checking for props, screen text, pacing and dialogue timing across cuts.
Its quality claims are BFL's own preference tests; independent testing is still thin.
flux-3-video.best_for: Talking scenes and long single takes with sound made in
flux-3-video.tip: Write it like a director: subject, action, camera move, light, then the spoken line in quotes and the sounds you want. Keep dialogue short for short clips.

gemini-omni-1.1.summary: Google's newest video model (Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, 2026). Short clips with sound from words, a start frame, a start and end frame, or up to 10 reference pictures, with physics grounded in real-world knowledge.
good: Sound is made with the picture; describe what you want to hear and it follows.
Convincing environments and physics: water, weather, objects reacting to each other.
Time events with timecodes in the prompt ('[0-3s] ... [3-6s]') and they land where you put them.
A cheap draft size lets you test ideas, then re-run the winner bigger.
Start-and-end-frame mode makes smooth transitions for the Board.
limits: Refuses real people: won't work from a real person's photo or likeness. The Studio marks it 'no real people'.
Renders at 720p; the larger sizes are upscaled, not extra detail.
In tests, characters glitched in motion and faces changed between angles.
Reference pictures can't be combined with a start or end frame.
gemini-omni-1.1.best_for: Fast clips with sound and good physics; transitions between two frames
gemini-omni-1.1.tip: Bind each reference picture in the prompt as <IMAGE_REF_0>, <IMAGE_REF_1> and so on. Add 'single unbroken shot, no scene cuts' for one take. Draft at the smallest size.

kling-o3.summary: Kling O3 (Video 3.0 Omni), the current model in Kling's 'O' line, which is built to work from references and to edit footage. In this entry it writes a clip from words or animates a still, with optional sound. A sibling of Kling 3.0 Pro, not a replacement.
good: Believable physics: water, cloth and bodies move with weight
Speaks more languages than Kling 3.0: English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Spanish
With a still attached it can end on an end frame, bridging two Board keyframes
Follows detailed scene directions, including the camera move and lighting
limits: Its Omni strength, working from your kit pictures, isn't used here: this entry takes no reference pictures
No 'things to avoid' list when animating a still
Takes a few minutes per clip
For plain generation it overlaps Kling 3.0 Pro, so try both on a key shot rather than assuming one wins
kling-o3.best_for: A second Kling flagship take, and dialogue beyond English and Chinese
kling-o3.tip: If the same person or product must appear across shots, pick a reference-to-video model; this entry can't take kit pictures.

grok-imagine-video-1.5.summary: xAI's Grok Imagine Video 1.5. Makes clips with sound from words, or animates a start frame (and can end on an end frame). Quick, with a wide choice of lengths and frame shapes.
good: Quick turnaround for video, so it suits trying many directions.
Sound in the same pass: ambience, effects, music and dialogue.
From a start frame it animates your picture faithfully instead of reinventing it.
Cheap at its draft size, so tests cost little.
limits: Reviewers saw odd movement, weaker physics and unpredictable explosions and impacts than the best models.
Voices can sound like flat narration, and continuity breaks down across multi-shot scenes.
Adding an end frame caps the size at 720p; full HD works only from a start frame alone.
Its own default is the smallest size; choose a bigger one for anything you'll show.
grok-imagine-video-1.5.best_for: Quick social clips with sound; animating a still faithfully
grok-imagine-video-1.5.tip: Put the key action first: it renders early beats early and can miss details at the end of a prompt. Name the sounds you want.

luma-ray-3-2.summary: Luma's current video model (Ray 3.2). Cinematic silent clips from words or a start frame, and it can land on an end frame. Known for smooth camera moves and subjects that hold together.
good: Smooth, cinematic camera moves and motion that stays coherent across the clip.
Start frame plus end frame for guided transitions; good for Board shots.
Luma says it plans the shot before rendering, which helps prompt following and physics.
Wide choice of frame shapes, including cinema widescreen.
limits: No sound; add music and effects separately.
Clips are 5 or 10 seconds only.
No reference pictures, so a kit product only carries through via the start frame.
Independent reviews are thin so far; test it on your own shot before committing a spot.
luma-ray-3-2.best_for: Cinematic silent cutaways and Board shots between two keyframes
luma-ray-3-2.tip: Write it as a shot description: subject, action, light, camera move ('slow aerial push-in'). Avoid stacking unrelated actions in one short clip.

veo-3.1-fast.summary: The quicker, cheaper version of Veo 3.1. Same clips with sound, start frame and end frame, at a much lower cost; it doesn't take reference pictures.
good: Much cheaper than full Veo 3.1 with the same sound and frame controls.
Sound with the picture, including dialogue with matching mouths.
Start and end frames make it a cost-effective Board animator.
Accepts a things-to-avoid prompt and a seed for steering and repeating takes.
limits: Refuses real people: won't work from a real person's photo or likeness. The Studio marks it 'no real people'.
No reference pictures; to hold a kit product, start from a keyframe or use full Veo 3.1.
A step below full Veo 3.1 on fine texture and busy scenes.
Short clips only, landscape or vertical only.
veo-3.1-fast.best_for: Board shots and drafts with sound on a budget

seedance-2.0-fast.summary: A quicker, cheaper version of Seedance 2.0. 'Fast' trades a little quality for speed and price. It has the same inputs and sound but stops below full HD, so it's for drafts and social clips.
good: Sound made with the picture: speech, effects, music.
Same toolkit as Seedance 2.0: start and end frames, reference pictures, several shots in one clip.
Much cheaper than full Seedance 2.0, so trying several takes is affordable.
limits: No full HD, so it's for drafts and phone screens rather than big screens.
Still several minutes a take, despite the name.
Blocks photos of real people's faces, as a start frame or as a reference picture.
Can't mix a start frame with reference pictures in one take. An end frame needs a start frame too.
seedance-2.0-fast.best_for: Social clips with sound, and drafting a Seedance shot cheaply
seedance-2.0-fast.tip: Name every reference in the prompt: 'image 1 is the bottle, image 2 is the kitchen'. Pictures you don't mention may be ignored.

seedance-2.0-mini.summary: The smallest, cheapest Seedance 2.0. 'Mini' is a slimmed-down copy of the full model. It's built for trying lots of variations quickly, then remaking the winners on a bigger Seedance.
good: The cheapest way to get Seedance 2.0's sound, multi-shot clips and reference pictures.
Good for testing many prompt, framing and motion ideas before paying for a full render.
Start frames, end frames, reference pictures and sound all work.
limits: Draft quality: lower resolution and less detail than full Seedance 2.0 or 2.5.
Blocks photos of real people's faces, in start frames and in reference pictures.
Keep to one or two characters a scene. With more, faces start to drift.
Only certain clip lengths are allowed, fewer than on the other Seedance 2.x models.
seedance-2.0-mini.best_for: Cheap Seedance drafts and lots of social variations
seedance-2.0-mini.tip: There's no 'avoid' box. Ask for what you want instead: 'stable face, same outfit throughout, natural hands'.

minimax-h3.summary: MiniMax's newest video model, also called Hailuo 3, from mid-2026. It makes very sharp clips at a film frame rate from words. Attach a start frame and it animates that instead, with an optional end frame.
good: Very sharp: it renders above full HD directly rather than enlarging afterwards.
Does what you write and only that, so precise direction pays off.
From a start frame it keeps your composition, light and product detail as things move. Add an end frame for a set transition.
Good at legible on-screen text and brand marks, though you should still check the spelling.
limits: No reference pictures in this mode. For a kit, use H3 Reference to Video.
Sound can't be switched on or steered here.
It won't invent a camera move. If you don't name one, expect a static camera.
Faces and objects can drift in the longest takes. Slow: several minutes, longer with a start frame.
minimax-h3.best_for: Sharp, precisely directed shots, and animating approved stills
minimax-h3.tip: Write one flowing sentence like a director: camera move, subject, action, setting, light, mood. With a start frame, describe only the motion, not what's already in the picture.

minimax-h3-max-turbo.summary: A speed-tuned H3. fal built 'H3 Max' from MiniMax's H3 with MiniMax, and 'Turbo' is a faster, cheaper version of that. Clips come back in well under a minute, at lower resolution than H3.
good: By far the quickest video model in this group, so it's good for trying lots of shots fast.
Follows specific briefs closely: one subject, one action, one camera move.
Start and end frames both work, for controlled transitions.
Legible titles and moving text when you quote the exact words.
Cheap per take.
limits: Below full HD. It's for exploring, not for the final sharp version (use H3 for that).
No reference pictures.
With a start frame the clip takes the picture's shape and ignores the shape setting.
An end frame only works together with a start frame.
minimax-h3-max-turbo.best_for: Fast, cheap exploration of many shots before the final render
minimax-h3-max-turbo.tip: Give it a start frame where something is about to move: a jug mid-tilt, a hand reaching out. It animates best when the motion is already implied.

ltx-2.5-fast.summary: The quick tier of Lightricks' LTX 2.5. Writes a clip from words or animates a still, with sound made alongside. It goes larger and longer than the Pro tier and turns clips round fast, so it suits drafts and volume.
good: Quick for a video model, so you can try several versions of a shot
Makes sound with the picture; lines written in quotes are spoken
Start frame and end frame, so it can join two Board keyframes
Can render very large frames for finishing, bigger than most models here
Designed to cut between a few shots in one clip and keep the same character across the cut
limits: Wide or tall frames only: no square or 4:5
The largest sizes and smoothest frame rates only allow clips up to 10 seconds
No seed, so you can't recreate a take exactly
Words on screen aren't reliable; add titles and logos in the edit
ltx-2.5-fast.best_for: Fast drafts and volume, and large-frame clips with sound
ltx-2.5-fast.tip: Keep 2K and 4K clips to 10 seconds or less; longer ones at those sizes are refused. Describe the sound you want, and put dialogue in quotes.

pixverse-v6.summary: PixVerse's current flagship (2026). Writes a clip from words or animates a still, with optional sound, and can move from a start frame to an end frame. Quick and one of the cheaper clips here.
good: Quick and low cost, so you can try several takes of a shot
Start-and-end-frame transitions, so it can bridge two Board keyframes
Wide choice of frame shapes, including ultra-wide cinema
Repeatable takes with a seed, plus a 'things to avoid' list
Makes ambience, effects and music in the same pass
limits: Reads more polished and stylized than photoreal; Kling is the stronger choice for high-end realism
Generated voices can be miscast (wrong gender, robotic), so check every line of dialogue
With a start frame, the picture's shape sets the frame and the aspect setting is ignored
pixverse-v6.best_for: Cheap, quick takes and start-to-end-frame transitions
pixverse-v6.tip: Draft at a low resolution to find the take, then re-run the same seed at a larger size. Ask for ambience and effects rather than dialogue.

p-video-2-pro.summary: Pruna's faster version of MiniMax's H3 video model. It makes film-style clips with sound from words, or from a start frame and an optional end frame. A quick, low-cost way to get shots with sound.
good: Every clip comes with sound made alongside the picture: effects, ambience and speech
Start frame and end frame let you set where a shot begins and where it lands
Quick and inexpensive for a clip with sound
Built on MiniMax's recent H3 video model, tuned by Pruna to run faster
limits: Top resolution is lower than most video models here: fine for drafts and social, soft on a big screen
The Studio shows no sound switch, but clips arrive with sound; mute it in the edit if you don't want it
Sound lands best with one clear action and one clear sound; busy scenes muddle the audio
With a start frame, the frame sets the shape and the aspect setting is ignored
p-video-2-pro.best_for: Quick, cheap shots with sound for drafts and social
p-video-2-pro.tip: Write the sound after the picture: 'Sound: rain on the roof, a distant dog.' Keep to one action and one sound per clip.

wan3.0-video-prime.summary: The faster tier of Wan 3.0: the same inputs, sound and long takes, returned sooner. It costs more per second than standard Wan 3.0, so it buys speed, not savings.
good: Everything Wan 3.0 does: words, start frame, end frame, reference pictures, and sound in one pass.
Noticeably quicker turnaround than standard Wan 3.0, for previews and client reviews.
Single takes of up to half a minute.
Sound follows the action closely; write the effects you want into the prompt.
limits: Dearer per second than standard Wan 3.0, despite sitting with the fast-and-cheap picks.
Shares Wan 3.0's faults: unasked-for camera cuts and weak text inside the frame.
Still minutes per clip, not seconds.
With a start frame or reference attached, the shape comes from the picture.
wan3.0-video-prime.best_for: Wan 3.0 quality when you need the take back sooner
wan3.0-video-prime.tip: Draft here at low resolution while the brief is moving; make finals on standard Wan 3.0 if budget matters more than waiting.

ltx-2.5-pro.summary: The higher-quality tier of Lightricks' LTX 2.5. Writes a clip from words or animates a still, with sound, and can cut between a few connected shots in one clip. Trades the Fast tier's speed and size for cleaner detail.
good: Tuned for cleaner faces, textures and fast motion than the Fast tier
Can render a few connected shots in one clip, keeping the character and voice across cuts
Speaks lines written in quotes, with matching ambience and music
Start frame and end frame, good for Board shots between two keyframes
Quicker than most premium video models here
limits: Clips are 6, 8 or 10 seconds only
Wide or tall frames only: no square
No seed and no 'things to avoid' list
Words on screen aren't reliable; add titles in the edit
ltx-2.5-pro.best_for: Polished short shots with sound, including simple multi-shot sequences
ltx-2.5-pro.tip: Write one present-tense paragraph: the shot, the action, the camera move in its own clause, then the sound. For a cut, say 'cut to' and describe the new framing.

sora-2.summary: OpenAI's standard Sora 2 video model: clips with synced sound from words or a start frame. OpenAI retired the Sora 2 API on 24 September 2026 (its deprecations page confirms it), so runs are likely to fail.
good: Believable physics and motion; reviewers found it strong on cause and effect.
Synced sound and dialogue in the same pass.
Longer takes than many models here.
limits: Retired by OpenAI on 24 Sept 2026: expect runs to fail. Use Veo 3.1 instead.
Rejects start frames that show a human face, and refuses real people.
The start frame must match the clip's exact size and shape, or the take fails or distorts.
Lower resolution than Sora 2 Pro; no end frame, reference pictures or seed.
sora-2.best_for: Physics-driven shots with sound, if it still runs
sora-2.tip: Try a short take first to see whether it still runs. If it fails, Veo 3.1 Fast is the nearest budget replacement with sound.

kling-3-standard.summary: The Standard tier of Kling 3.0: the same model and controls as Pro, run on a lighter quality budget. Writes a clip from words or animates a still, with sound. Use it to work out a shot before rendering the keeper in Pro.
good: Same prompt-following and natural motion as Kling 3.0 Pro, so drafts predict the final
Makes sound in the same pass: ambience, effects and short dialogue
With a still attached it can also land on an end frame, for Board shots between two keyframes
Takes camera directions (dolly, crane, handheld) and a 'things to avoid' list
limits: Less fine detail and steadiness than Pro; re-run the chosen take in Pro for delivery
Speech is made in English or Chinese only
No reference pictures, so it can't keep a kit person or product exact across shots
Not a quick sketch tool: a few minutes per clip
kling-3-standard.best_for: Working out Kling 3.0 shots before a final Pro render

hailuo-2.3.summary: MiniMax's late-2025 video model, praised for body motion and facial acting. It makes silent clips from words or a start frame. MiniMax H3 is newer and sharper, but 2.3 is cheaper and quicker.
good: Natural body movement, even in dance, sport and crowded scenes.
Expressive faces: small changes of expression land believably, which helps reaction and testimonial-style shots.
Holds a style for the whole clip: anime, illustration, ink painting.
Carries out a specific action without inventing stray objects.
Cheaper and quicker than H3.
limits: No sound. Add it in the edit.
No end frame. For start-and-end control, use H3.
Clips are 6 or 10 seconds only, and 10 seconds only at the lower resolution.
Without a start frame you can't choose the shape.
hailuo-2.3.best_for: Character performance and expressive faces in silent shots
hailuo-2.3.tip: Describe the movement precisely: 'turns her head slowly toward camera and smiles'. It rewards specific motion verbs more than mood words.

runway-gen4-turbo.summary: Runway's fast, cheaper Gen-4 model. It only animates a start frame: give it a still and describe the motion. A quick, dependable silent Board animator.
good: Fast for video, so you can run several takes quickly.
Keeps the look of your start frame and moves people, animals and objects naturally.
Takes camera directions (pan, tilt, push-in) and style cues in plain words.
Many frame shapes, including cinema widescreen, and a seed for repeat takes.
limits: Needs a start frame; it can't make a clip from words alone.
No sound, no end frame, no reference pictures.
Clips are 5 or 10 seconds only, at a lower resolution than the newest models.
runway-gen4-turbo.best_for: Quick, silent Board shots from a keyframe
runway-gen4-turbo.tip: Describe only the motion and the camera; the start frame already sets the look, and re-describing it can make the clip drift.

happyhorse-1.1.summary: Version 1.1 of Alibaba's HappyHorse. It makes picture and sound together, with mouths matching speech in several languages, from words, a start frame or reference pictures. Its predecessor topped a public blind-vote video leaderboard at launch.
good: Picture and sound made in one pass: dialogue, ambience and effects line up with the action.
Mouths match the speech in several languages, including English, Mandarin, Japanese, Korean, German and French.
Holds characters, products and places from reference pictures (your kit) across shots.
Alibaba says 1.1 improves shot control, motion, physics and consistency over 1.0.
Cinematic look: smooth motion, warm grading, shallow focus.
limits: No end frame: it starts from a picture but can't land on a set final frame.
Can't follow your own voice track; it writes its own audio.
Independent tests are scarce; most claims come from Alibaba and resellers.
One of the pricier clips here.
happyhorse-1.1.best_for: Talking-character spots and kit-based shots that need speech with matching mouths
happyhorse-1.1.tip: Put the spoken line in quotes and say who speaks it. Short prompts get expanded by the model, so write a full description when you need exact control.

pixverse-5-transition.summary: PixVerse V5's transition mode: give it a start frame and an end frame and it animates from one to the other. The older PixVerse way to bridge two Board keyframes or morph one picture into another.
good: Built for one job: moving from one still to another
Handy for scene-to-scene bridges, product reveals and logo-to-product morphs
Follows a short description of the movement between the two pictures
Quick enough to try a few versions
limits: No sound in the Studio
Clips are 5 or 8 seconds only
If the two stills differ in framing, light or subject size, expect a visible morph rather than a natural move
Older generation: PixVerse V6 also does start-and-end-frame clips, with sound
pixverse-5-transition.best_for: Simple morphs and bridges between two matching keyframes
pixverse-5-transition.tip: Give it two stills shot with the same lens, light and subject scale, and describe the movement between them rather than the pictures themselves.

wan2.7.summary: Wan 2.7 (spring 2026). It writes a clip from words, or animates a start frame toward an optional end frame. Sharp, steady motion at a lower price per clip than Wan 3.0.
good: Start frame plus end frame: give it two stills and it makes the move between them, ideal for Board shots and product reveals.
Steadier motion and less flicker than earlier Wan; skin, fabric and light hold up in close-ups.
Reviewers found it handles busy scenes with several subjects well.
Lengths from a couple of seconds up to fifteen.
Cheaper per clip than Wan 3.0.
limits: Superseded by Wan 3.0, which runs twice as long and takes reference pictures.
No reference pictures, so it can't hold a cast or product from the kit.
Fast action can still smear or wobble.
Start and end frames need the same angle and scale, or the move between them turns into a strange morph.
wan2.7.best_for: Animating a Board keyframe toward a set final frame at a modest price
wan2.7.tip: Write the prompt as motion directions ('camera slowly pushes in, she turns to the window') and keep to one or two actions per shot.

pixverse-v6-extend.summary: Extend for PixVerse V6: adds new seconds after the end of a clip you already have, continuing its motion, light and camera. Optional sound for the added part.
good: Picks up the clip's motion, lighting and camera so the join is hard to spot
Can add just a beat or a longer multi-step sequence
Follows a literal 'what happens next' prompt, including a new hand or object entering
Optional ambience and effects sound for the new part
Repeatable with a seed once you find a direction you like
limits: Sometimes unreliable: twice came back 'temporarily unavailable' in our tests (not charged)
Only adds time after the end; it can't change anything already in the clip
The source clip can be 30 seconds and 50 MB at most
Generated voices can be miscast, so keep dialogue out of extensions
pixverse-v6-extend.best_for: Extend: a shot that ended a beat too soon
pixverse-v6-extend.tip: Name one concrete next action per short extension, and upload the source at the size you want back. If it's unavailable, try again later or use FLUX 3 Extend.

flux-3-extend-video.summary: Adds new seconds after the end of a clip (the Studio's Extend), carrying on the framing, motion and sound. Part of Black Forest Labs' FLUX 3.
good: Picks up from the clip's last moment, so the shot carries on rather than restarting.
Makes matching sound for the new section.
Good for reveals and next beats: pull-backs, crane-ups, a character finishing an action.
Worked first time in our own tests.
limits: Can't change anything already in the clip; it only adds time after the end.
It works from the tail end of your clip, so things shown earlier may not carry over.
No reference pictures, so a product that left the frame can't be brought back exactly.
flux-3-extend-video.best_for: Lengthening a shot you like without a reshoot
flux-3-extend-video.tip: Describe only what happens next (action, camera move, sound), not the scene you already have. One clear beat per extension works best.

gemini-omni-1.1-video-extend.summary: The Extend mode of Google's Gemini Omni 1.1. Give it a short clip and it adds a continuation after the end, carrying on the camera move, the subject, the light and the sound.
good: Reads the end of your clip, so the camera move, subject and light carry across the join.
Makes sound for the new section to match.
The prompt is optional: leave it to continue naturally, or say where the action goes.
Chain several runs to build a longer shot.
limits: Refuses real people, so it won't extend real footage of a person. The Studio marks it 'no real people'.
Your clip must be 10 seconds or less, and each run adds at most 10 seconds.
It reworks the last few frames of your clip to hide the join, so the original ending changes slightly.
The larger sizes are upscaled from 720p.
gemini-omni-1.1-video-extend.best_for: Extend: add a few seconds to an AI-made or people-free clip
gemini-omni-1.1-video-extend.tip: Works best when the clip ends mid-motion: a push-in, a pan, someone walking. Say how camera and sound should carry on; 'extend this' alone gives weak results.

runway-gen4-aleph.summary: Runway's video editor (Aleph). Give it a clip and an instruction and it reworks the footage: change season, weather or light, add, remove or replace objects, or show the scene from a new camera angle.
good: Restyles real footage convincingly: season, weather, time of day, overall look.
Adds, removes or replaces objects while keeping the motion consistent frame to frame.
Can make a new camera angle of the same scene from your clip.
Short instructions like 'make it winter with snow' work well.
limits: Only the first 5 seconds of your clip are used, and the file must be under 16 MB.
No sound, and slow: a few minutes a take.
Fine detail such as fingers and lip movement can still need fixing afterwards.
runway-gen4-aleph.best_for: Change: restyle or alter the opening seconds of a clip
runway-gen4-aleph.tip: Trim the clip to the exact moment you need before you run it, since it only reads the opening seconds.

kling-o3-video2video-edit.summary: Kling O3's Change tool: rewrites part of an existing clip from a written instruction while keeping the movement. Swap a product, outfit or background, or restyle the scene, guided by reference pictures.
good: Strong at swapping a product or wardrobe item when you attach a reference picture of it
Keeps the original movement and camera; you describe only what changes
Several reference pictures can steer the item, the look or the setting
Background swaps and restyles (season, time of day, look) from words
limits: Slow: several minutes per clip in our tests
Takes 3 to 10 seconds of footage; a longer stretch makes nothing, so set In and Out first
Won't swap in an item without a reference picture of it; that run failed in our test
The source clip must be at least 720 pixels wide, so small vertical clips are refused
kling-o3-video2video-edit.best_for: Change: swap a product, outfit or background in real footage
kling-o3-video2video-edit.tip: Call the pictures @Image1, @Image2 in the order attached, and say what stays: 'Replace the jacket with @Image1. Keep the face, motion and background.'

wan2.7-videoedit.summary: Alibaba's Wan 2.7 clip editor. Give it a short clip and a written instruction and it restyles or changes the footage while keeping the motion. One of the Studio's Change options.
good: Worked from words alone in our test and returned the whole clip, edited.
Keeps the original timing and camera move while changing the look, season, materials or objects.
Takes long instructions, so you can spell out several changes at once.
Can copy the look of a style picture onto the footage.
limits: Source clips must be short (about 2 to 10 seconds); trim longer footage first.
You pay for the length of the source clip as well as the result.
Slow and one of the pricier ways to Change a clip: many minutes a take.
wan2.7-videoedit.best_for: Changing a short clip's look or contents from a written instruction
wan2.7-videoedit.tip: Say what to change and what to keep ('make it winter, keep the car and driver unchanged'). Try FLUX 3 Video Edit first for simple restyles; it's far cheaper and quicker.

flux-3-video-edit.summary: Black Forest Labs' clip editor: give it a clip and one instruction and it changes that one thing, keeping the motion, camera and timing. A cheap, fast first try for the Studio's Change tool.
good: Cheap and quick: in our test it restyled a full-HD clip in about a minute.
Keeps the original motion, camera move and timing; only what you name changes.
Restyles season, time of day, weather or the whole look, with no mask needed.
Can add or remove objects, put steady text on a wall, or rewrite a spoken line with mouths that follow.
limits: Takes no reference picture, so it can't swap in your exact product or wardrobe item; words only.
Clips must be 15 seconds or shorter, and the result comes back at 720p even from a sharper source.
A silent clip stays silent, so dialogue changes need a clip that already has sound.
Stacking several changes in one instruction is less reliable than one at a time.
flux-3-video-edit.best_for: Quick restyles: season, time of day, weather or overall look
flux-3-video-edit.tip: Name only the change and what must stay: 'make it winter with snow on the ground, keep the camera and timing'. For a product or wardrobe swap, use Kling O3 edit with a reference picture.

modify-video.summary: Luma's Modify Video. Restyles or reimagines a clip you shot while keeping the actors' movement, expressions and lip movement. Settings run from a faithful touch-up to a full reimagining.
good: Keeps the performance: body movement, faces and lip movement carry through the restyle.
Strength settings from subtle grade-and-relight to a complete new world.
Attach a restyled version of the first frame and it carries that look through the clip.
Output keeps your clip's own size.
limits: Slow: several minutes a take.
The source clip must be under 30 seconds and 100 MB.
Struggles with heavy camera shake, very fast action, dark or blurry footage and crowded scenes.
modify-video.best_for: Change: restyle real footage while keeping the actor's performance
modify-video.tip: For a big look change, restyle a still of the clip's first frame in an image model, then attach it as the start frame; Modify carries that look through.

clarityai-crystal-upscaler.summary: Clarity AI's faithful upscaler, and the Studio's default. It makes a picture bigger and sharper while keeping it as it is (same faces, same lettering) instead of inventing new detail.
good: Faithful: faces, skin and product details still look like the original
Clean results without the 'painted' look creative upscalers can leave
Built for portraits, product shots and print enlargements
Quick
limits: It won't rebuild what isn't there: a badly blurred or damaged picture stays weak
No prompt, so you can't steer it
Costs more per picture than the basic upscalers here
clarityai-crystal-upscaler.best_for: Enlarging finished pictures for print without changing them
clarityai-crystal-upscaler.tip: Use it on the final pick, not every draft. If a face or texture really needs rebuilding, try a creative upscaler and compare the two.

topaz-image-upscale.summary: Topaz Labs' photo upscaler, from the same family as their Gigapixel software that many photographers use. Faithful by default: it enlarges, sharpens and cleans noise without redrawing the picture.
good: Faithful: keeps the picture as it is, just bigger, sharper and cleaner
Strong on real photographs, including old or noisy ones
Keeps a person's likeness on faces instead of inventing a new face
A long track record with professional photographers
limits: The Studio runs its general setting; Topaz's special modes for lettering, graphics or tiny sources aren't offered
Its face boost is off by default here, so very small faces stay soft
Can smooth away the painterly texture of AI art
Pricier than the basic upscalers
topaz-image-upscale.best_for: Enlarging real photographs faithfully for print
topaz-image-upscale.tip: For photos, Topaz or Crystal. For soft AI art where you want new detail invented, a creative upscaler suits better.

clarity-upscaler.summary: Clarity AI's open-source upscaler, known as the 'free Magnific alternative'. It's a creative upscaler: it enlarges and invents new fine detail, guided by a prompt. Cheap, but it can change faces and lettering.
good: Adds rich texture and crisp detail to soft or AI-made pictures
Very cheap for a creative upscaler
The Studio passes the take's own prompt, so the new detail fits the scene
Accepts 'things to avoid'
limits: Creative: it invents detail, so faces can change and small lettering can turn to gibberish
Built on an older SD 1.5-era engine; Clarity's newer Flux upscaler is in the list
Not for product shots or likenesses that must stay exact
clarity-upscaler.best_for: Adding detail to soft AI art cheaply
clarity-upscaler.tip: Compare it with the original at full size before using it: check eyes, hands, logos and lettering.

bria-increase-resolution.summary: Bria's faithful upscaler. It makes a picture larger while keeping it as it is, enhancing what's there rather than inventing new detail. Trained on licensed images only.
good: Faithful: enhances the existing detail instead of making up new detail
Keeps transparent backgrounds on cutouts and logos
Licensed-data training, a plus for commercial use
Cheap
limits: Can't rescue a blurry or tiny picture; it needs a clean source
No prompt or style control
Less dramatic than creative upscalers on soft AI art
bria-increase-resolution.best_for: Safe, faithful enlargement of product shots and cutouts
bria-increase-resolution.tip: Run it after a cutout: it keeps the transparent background.

bria-remove-background.summary: Bria's RMBG 2.0 background remover, the Studio's cutout tool. It lifts the subject onto a transparent background with soft, natural edges. Trained on licensed images.
good: Soft, clean edges on hair and fur instead of hard, jagged cut lines
One click: no prompt and no mask
Licensed-data training, safer for commercial cutouts
Fast and cheap
limits: It decides for itself what the subject is, and can keep or drop the wrong thing in a busy scene
Glass, reflections and very fine see-through edges are the hardest cases
Low-resolution pictures give rougher edges
bria-remove-background.tip: If it keeps or drops the wrong item, use Bria Guided Remove Background and say what to keep, e.g. 'only the chair'.

topaz-video-upscale.summary: Topaz Labs' video enhancer (Topaz Video AI). Faithful: it makes a clip larger and sharper and cleans noise and compression blocks, without redrawing the shot.
good: Faithful: keeps the clip as it is, just cleaner and larger
Cleans grain and compression blocks from older or web footage
A standard tool among editors for upscaling footage
Takes AI clips up to delivery size
limits: Source clips can be up to 45 seconds
By default it raises the frame rate to 60, which can make a filmic 24 fps clip look like TV video
Can't invent detail that isn't there: the waxy skin of AI clips gets sharper, not fixed
Slow: a couple of minutes a clip
topaz-video-upscale.best_for: Cleaning and enlarging finished clips for delivery
topaz-video-upscale.tip: Upscale only the takes that make the cut, and compare a few seconds with the original before you sign off. Watch the motion as well as the sharpness.

kandinsky-6-vsr.summary: The Kandinsky 6.0 video upscaler from Sber. No prompt: give it a short, soft clip and it rebuilds it larger and sharper without flicker. Works on AI clips and camera footage.
good: Rebuilds fine texture (feathers, fabric, foliage, skin) that goes mushy in small clips.
Stable from frame to frame: no shimmering or boiling detail.
Restores rather than invents, so framing and motion stay as they were.
Cheap for what it does.
limits: About 5 seconds at most (121 frames); longer clips are rejected, so trim first.
Slow: several minutes per clip.
Can't rescue heavy compression or noise; cleaner sources upscale better.
Its 2x and 4x settings need frame sizes that divide by 16; the 2.25x setting takes any size.
kandinsky-6-vsr.best_for: Finishing a short draft clip at full HD

bria-increase-video-resolution.summary: Bria's video upscaler. It enlarges a clip two or four times and keeps its frame rate, colour and sound. Trained on licensed data.
good: Faithful: keeps the shot, frame rate and sound as they were
Licensed-data training, a plus for commercial delivery
Cheaper per clip than Topaz
limits: Slow: a few minutes a clip
A straight enlargement: it doesn't promise the noise clean-up Topaz does
Output can't go past 8K, so enlarging an already large clip four times fails
bria-increase-video-resolution.best_for: Plain, faithful enlargement of a finished clip

fast-flux-schnell.summary: Segmind's speed-tuned copy of FLUX.1 Schnell, the 2024 'fast' version of FLUX ('schnell' is German for fast). Near-instant and nearly free; quality is draft level.
good: Among the cheapest and fastest pictures here, so you can test dozens of ideas.
Understands plain-sentence prompts better than older fast models.
Manages short words on signs reasonably for such a fast model.
limits: Two generations old: less detail and weaker prompt-following than FLUX 3 Klein.
No reference pictures and no size choice beyond shape.
Hands, faces and small text are hit and miss.
fast-flux-schnell.best_for: Throwaway idea sketches at almost no cost

bg-removal-v2.summary: Segmind's own quick background remover. One click gives a transparent cutout: a very cheap alternative to Bria's cutout for drafts.
good: Very fast and very cheap
No prompt or mask needed
Good enough for comps and layout mock-ups
limits: Segmind's page lists a non-commercial licence: use Bria Remove Background for anything we sell
No control over what counts as the subject
Older and far less documented than Bria's RMBG 2.0
bg-removal-v2.best_for: Fast cutouts for comps and mock-ups

face-to-many.summary: An open SDXL-era workflow that turns a face photo into a stylised character (3D cartoon, emoji, pixel art, video game, clay or toy) while keeping a likeness.
good: Keeps a recognisable likeness while restyling the face
Fun, quick and cheap novelty looks
Accepts 'things to avoid'
limits: The Studio doesn't offer its style picker, so it uses its default 3D style
Older SDXL generation: needs a clear close-up face, and hands and full bodies come out poorly
Novelty looks only, not realistic pictures
face-to-many.best_for: Playful stylised avatars from a face photo

nano-banana-2.summary: Google's Nano Banana 2 (Gemini image model): fast, photoreal pictures from words, and edits or blends from up to 14 reference pictures. Replaced by Nano Banana 2.1.
good: Photoreal, well-lit pictures quickly.
Keeps a subject's look consistent across a series of pictures.
Edits and multi-picture composites from plain instructions.
Has a seed.
limits: Superseded by Nano Banana 2.1, which improves text, layout and very wide frames.
Can't make transparent cut-outs.
Behind Nano Banana Pro on dense, detailed briefs.
nano-banana-2.best_for: Quick photoreal stills when 2.1 isn't to hand

gpt-image-2.summary: OpenAI's April 2026 image model: photoreal pictures with very accurate text in many scripts, plus edits from attached pictures. Replaced by GPT Image 2.5.
good: Text in many scripts (Latin, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hindi) renders cleanly enough to use.
Handles counts, colours, positions and exact wording in a single prompt.
Edits from attached pictures: relight, swap a background, change copy.
limits: Can't make transparent backgrounds.
Edits drift after one or two passes: colours burn out and people degrade.
Weak at physical puzzles (reflections, origami) and dense repeating detail.
No seed.

nano-banana.summary: The original Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, 2025). Quick, cheap edits that keep a face or product true to the photo, with up to three reference pictures.
good: Very fast and cheap.
Keeps a person's or product's look when you change the background, clothes or setting.
Composites up to three pictures into one scene.
limits: Older generation: text, detail and size fall well short of Nano Banana 2.1 and Pro.
Only three reference pictures, no size choice and no seed.
nano-banana.best_for: Cheap, quick photo edits and background swaps

esrgan.summary: ESRGAN, a classic open upscaler from 2018 research. Faithful and very cheap: it enlarges and sharpens without a prompt, but it's an old generation.
good: Faithful: it doesn't redraw the picture or invent new objects
One of the cheapest and fastest upscalers here
Fine for quick enlargements of drafts and web pictures
limits: Old generation: textures can look over-sharpened or plastic next to Crystal or Topaz
Segmind's page lists a non-commercial licence; prefer another upscaler for pictures we license
No face repair, so small faces stay soft or look odd

seedance-2.0.summary: ByteDance's early-2026 flagship, which put sound and several shots into a single clip. It's still excellent and is the only Seedance here that renders 4K directly, but Seedance 2.5 now makes longer takes.
good: Sound made with the picture, with mouths matching the speech in many languages.
Several shots in one clip with natural cuts: 'Shot 1: … Shot 2: …'.
Reference pictures, start frame and end frame for keeping people, products and looks consistent.
Strong, believable motion and camera work. It topped public video leaderboards when it came out.
Renders 4K directly, without an upscaler.
limits: Blocks photos of real people's faces, as a start frame or as a reference picture.
Busy scenes can break: crowds, handshakes and fast action can show warped fingers or bent limbs.
Several minutes a take, and shorter takes than Seedance 2.5.
Can't mix a start frame with reference pictures. An end frame needs a start frame too.
seedance-2.0.best_for: Multi-shot clips with sound when you want 4K straight from the model
seedance-2.0.tip: Call kit pictures 'image 1', 'image 2' in the prompt and say what each one does: 'the woman from image 1 walks into the café from image 2'.

flux-schnell.summary: FLUX.1 Schnell, the 2024 fast, open version of Black Forest Labs' first FLUX family ('schnell' is German for fast). Very cheap and quick; fine for rough ideas, not finals.
good: Among the cheapest and fastest pictures here.
Understands plain-sentence prompts better than older fast models.
Offers a larger size than Fast Flux.1 Schnell.
limits: Two generations old: less detail and weaker prompt-following than FLUX 3 Klein.
No reference pictures.
Hands, faces and small text are hit and miss.
