flux-schnell.best_for: Rough idea sketches at almost no cost

flux-2-klein-4b.summary: The smallest FLUX.2 model ('Klein' is German for small), built to run in about a second on an ordinary graphics card. Makes pictures from words or blends reference pictures, cheaply and fast.
good: Very fast and cheap.
Takes up to ten reference pictures to blend or edit from.
Accepts a 'things to avoid' prompt.
limits: The smallest of FLUX.2, so less detail and weaker prompt-following than the bigger tiers.
Superseded by FLUX 3 Klein, which adds box layout and larger sizes for about the same money.
No size choice in the Studio beyond shape.

flux-2-klein-9b.summary: The larger of the two FLUX.2 Klein models: a little more detail and better prompt-following than the 4B version, still very fast and cheap.
good: Very fast and cheap.
More detail than Klein 4B for a small price step.
Takes up to ten reference pictures to blend or edit from.
Accepts a 'things to avoid' prompt.
limits: Still a small model: behind FLUX.2 Pro and FLUX 3 on detail and complex scenes.
Superseded by FLUX 3 Klein, which adds box layout and larger sizes.
No size choice in the Studio beyond shape.
flux-2-klein-9b.best_for: Quick, cheap drafts with a little more polish

seedance-1.5-pro.summary: ByteDance's late-2025 model, the first Seedance to make sound with the picture. It's now one of the cheapest and quickest clips with sound here, though Seedance 2.0 and 2.5 look and follow direction better.
good: Sound and picture made together, with mouths roughly matching speech.
One of the cheapest and quickest clips with sound in the Studio.
Start and end frames for controlled transitions.
Takes emotional and camera direction reasonably well for its price.
limits: No reference pictures, so it can't hold a kit product or person beyond the start frame.
Older generation: less detail and weaker motion than Seedance 2.0 and 2.5.
An end frame only works together with a start frame.
seedance-1.5-pro.best_for: Cheap test clips with sound, or quick start-to-end transitions
seedance-1.5-pro.tip: Write it like a shot list with the sound last: setting, subject, action, camera, light, then the audio ('clear female voice, soft room tone').

sam3-image.summary: Meta's Segment Anything 3 for stills. It doesn't make pictures: it finds and outlines the things you name ('red car', 'person in a hat') and returns masks: black-and-white outlines of each one.
good: Finds every instance of a named thing from plain words.
Precise outlines, useful for cut-outs or marking an area to repaint.
Very fast and almost free.
limits: Returns masks and overlays, not a finished picture.
Vague words give poor masks; use specific nouns like 'red sedan'.
sam3-image.best_for: A mask or cut-out of a named object in a still

seedream-4.summary: The earlier Seedream generation, known for clean text and layout and for large output. It's still cheap and capable, but Seedream 4.5 does the same jobs better.
good: Clear text and balanced layouts for posters, banners and simple infographics.
Large output, up to print size.
Edits an attached picture from plain words, and blends reference pictures.
Quick and cheap for a still.
limits: Older generation: Seedream 4.5 and 5 beat it on realism and on keeping a person consistent.
Fixed shapes only. It won't automatically match the shape of a picture you attach.
No seed, so you can't repeat an exact picture.
seedream-4.best_for: Cheap poster and banner drafts with readable text

sdxl1.0-juggernaut-lightning.summary: A fast version of Juggernaut XL, a popular photo-style community model built on SDXL by the creator KandooAI. One of the cheapest, quickest ways in the Studio to get a realistic-looking picture.
good: Photo-style people, places and products in a couple of seconds
Among the cheapest pictures in the Studio, so you can try lots of ideas
Decent lighting and skin for an SDXL-era model
Takes an 'avoid' list, and a seed gives you the same picture again
limits: Older generation: hands, crowds and long prompts go wrong far more often than with today's flagships
Can't write legible text in the picture
Square pictures only
The speed shortcut costs a little detail and variety compared with the full model
sdxl1.0-juggernaut-lightning.best_for: Cheap, fast photo-style drafts and mood frames
sdxl1.0-juggernaut-lightning.tip: Keep prompts short and concrete: subject, setting, light, lens. Run several takes and keep the best one; each costs very little.

gpt-image-1.summary: OpenAI's first GPT Image model (2025), words-to-picture only here. Decent text and transparent backgrounds for its day, long since overtaken by GPT Image 1.5, 2 and 2.5.
good: Follows detailed prompts well for its time.
Transparent backgrounds for cut-outs.
Reasonable short text in pictures.
limits: Older generation: slower, dearer and less accurate than GPT Image 2.5.
Takes no reference pictures in this version.
Only three frame shapes and a modest top size.
Pictures often lean warm or yellowish.
gpt-image-1.best_for: Rarely: GPT Image 2.5 Flare does this job better

sd1.5-realisticvision.summary: Realistic Vision, a well-known Stable Diffusion 1.5 photo-style model by the community creator SG_161222. By 2023 standards its portraits looked like photos; today it's mainly a very cheap way to get that older look.
good: Natural-looking portraits and headshots for its age
Very cheap and fast
Responds well to an 'avoid' list (blurry, extra fingers, cartoon)
A seed gives you the same picture again
limits: SD 1.5 generation: weak hands, odd anatomy, and it can't spell
Small, square pictures in the Studio; upscale before any real use
Needs detailed prompts and loses track of scenes with several people
sd1.5-realisticvision.best_for: Cheap portrait drafts in an older photo style
sd1.5-realisticvision.tip: Segmind suggests pairing it with an upscaler. Run the keeper through one of the Studio's upscalers before you show it to anyone.

sd1.5-reliberate.summary: Reliberate, an Stable Diffusion 1.5 community model from the makers of the popular Deliberate model, tuned toward a photographic look. A cheap legacy option for portrait and character tests.
good: Photo-like portraits from short, simple prompts
Very cheap and fast
Takes an 'avoid' list and a seed
limits: SD 1.5 generation: hands, anatomy and text are unreliable
Small, square pictures in the Studio
Struggles with busy scenes and more than one person
sd1.5-reliberate.best_for: Quick portrait or character tests on a tiny budget
sd1.5-reliberate.tip: Its makers say less is more: try a short, plain description before piling on detail.

flux-dev.summary: FLUX.1 Dev, the open middle tier of Black Forest Labs' 2024 FLUX.1 family and the base most community add-ons were trained on. Cheap and quick; decent everyday quality for its age.
good: Understands natural sentences and placement words like 'to the left of'.
Manages short words on signs and labels for its age.
Cheap and quick.
limits: Older generation: FLUX 3 Klein is better and costs about the same.
No reference pictures in this version.
Known for a glossy, waxy-skin 'AI look' and a recurring cleft chin on faces.
flux-dev.best_for: Cheap general pictures when you don't need the newest model

nomos-upscaler.summary: A community-trained photo upscaler (Nomos8k SPAN) that enlarges four times. Faithful and cheap: it aims for a natural look while cleaning noise, compression blocks and slight blur.
good: Faithful, natural-looking results on real photos
Cleans JPEG blocks, noise and mild blur as it enlarges
Cheap and quick
limits: Always enlarges four times, with no gentler setting
Tuned for photos; graphics, lettering and illustrations may come out less clean
No prompt and no face repair
nomos-upscaler.best_for: Cheap, natural four-times enlargement of real photos

sd1.5-juggernaut.summary: The Stable Diffusion 1.5 version of Juggernaut, KandooAI's photo-style community model, and the ancestor of the Juggernaut XL and Juggernaut Flux models also in the Studio. Kept for its price and older look.
good: Photo-style scenes and people at very low cost
Fast
Takes an 'avoid' list and a seed
limits: SD 1.5 generation: weak hands and anatomy, no readable text
Small, square pictures in the Studio
The newer Juggernaut models here are clearly better

grok-imagine-image.summary: xAI's first Grok Imagine image model. Pictures from words, or edits of up to three attached pictures, with a quick standard mode and a slower quality mode. Replaced by Grok Imagine Image 2.
good: Quick and economical for idea exploration.
Readable text when you put the words in quotes.
Edits from a plain instruction: restyle, swap a background, add an object.
Lots of tall and wide frame shapes.
limits: Superseded by Grok Imagine Image 2 on text, layout and editing.
Has no things-to-avoid prompt; say what you want instead ('sharp focus, clean background').
xAI's own notes say its commercial safety is looser than some rivals; review brand work.
grok-imagine-image.best_for: Quick concept stills and simple edits
grok-imagine-image.tip: Refer to attached pictures in the prompt as <IMAGE_0>, <IMAGE_1>, <IMAGE_2>.

face-detailer.summary: A Segmind workflow that finds the faces in a picture, repaints them with more detail and upscales the result. A repair tool for soft or warped faces in AI pictures.
good: Fixes mushy or distorted faces in AI pictures
Leaves the rest of the picture alone
Uses the prompt to guide the new face
limits: Creative: it repaints faces, so a real person's likeness can change
Needs a prompt; the Studio reuses the take's own, so a picture with no prompt may fail
An older workflow; not for real people whose likeness must be kept
face-detailer.best_for: Repairing soft or warped faces in AI pictures

juggernaut-pro-flux.summary: RunDiffusion's photoreal retune of FLUX, from the team behind the popular Juggernaut series. It aims to fix FLUX's plastic skin and cleft chin; cheap and quick.
good: More natural skin and organic textures than stock FLUX.1, which can look waxy.
Sharper fine detail and livelier contrast, per its makers.
Less of the 'FLUX chin' on portraits.
Cheap and quick.
limits: No reference pictures, so it can't keep a person or product.
Built on the older FLUX.1 generation; prompt-following and text are behind FLUX 3.
The improvement claims are the maker's own.
juggernaut-pro-flux.best_for: Cheap photoreal people and textures without the plastic look

segmind-vega.summary: Segmind's slimmed-down, faster copy of SDXL (2023). Very cheap square pictures; of interest mainly for speed and price.
good: One of the cheapest and fastest image models here
Accepts 'things to avoid'
Fine for rough concept sketches
limits: Old SDXL generation: weak hands, can't spell, misses parts of complex prompts
Square pictures only
Far behind current models in detail and realism
segmind-vega.best_for: Throwaway square sketches at the lowest cost

flux-2-pro.summary: The standard tier of FLUX.2 (late 2025) and Black Forest Labs' everyday production model. 'Pro' sits below Max (best prompt-following, web lookup). Photoreal, with up to ten reference pictures.
good: Dependable photoreal results at a moderate price: the workhorse of FLUX.2.
Keeps a person, product or style consistent across a set from up to ten reference pictures.
Handles text and logos far better than FLUX.1.
Has a seed for repeatable results.
limits: Superseded by FLUX 3, which adds box layout control and bigger files.
Text is good but less consistent than the specialists (Ideogram, Recraft).
No web lookup (that's Max), so real products and places can come out generic.
flux-2-pro.best_for: Consistent photoreal sets from reference pictures at a fair price

flux-1.1-pro.summary: FLUX 1.1 Pro (late 2024), the paid top model of the first FLUX generation: faster and sharper than FLUX.1 Pro. Still a solid photoreal all-rounder, but two generations old.
good: Follows natural sentences and placement words ('a red mug to the left of the books') well.
Readable short text when you put it in quotes.
Quick.
limits: Web-size output only.
Its one reference picture loosely steers the mood; it won't keep a product or face.
Two generations behind FLUX 3.
flux-1.1-pro.best_for: A quick, dependable photoreal picture when cost matters

nano-banana-2-lite.summary: Google's fastest, cheapest Nano Banana (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Image). Makes and edits pictures, and blends up to 14 reference pictures, in seconds, at one small size only.
good: Very quick, so it suits rapid ideas and many variations.
Edits and multi-picture composites like its bigger siblings.
Legible text and steady characters across quick runs.
Has a seed.
limits: One small size only: not for print or big crops.
Speed first: less detail than Nano Banana 2.1 or Pro.
Can't make transparent cut-outs.
nano-banana-2-lite.best_for: Fast rough keyframes and lots of cheap variations
nano-banana-2-lite.tip: Use it to find the composition, then re-run the keeper in Nano Banana 2.1 or Pro for the final.

wan2.7-image.summary: The standard tier of Alibaba's Wan 2.7 picture model: the same layout planning and multilingual text as Pro, at a lower price and smaller size. Can edit from one reference picture.
good: Puts things where the prompt says; good with crowded, many-part descriptions.
Clear text in about a dozen languages; its lettering scored top marks in a vendor's side-by-side.
Edits by instruction with one reference picture.
Cheaper and quicker than the Pro tier.
Takes exact colour tones for brand work.
limits: Smaller output than Pro; not for large prints.
One reference picture only.
In a vendor's close-up test, skin and eye detail was softer than Nano Banana Pro's.
wan2.7-image.best_for: Layout-heavy marketing images and labels at a moderate price
wan2.7-image.tip: Spell out positions ('logo top left, product centre, headline across the bottom') and put exact words in quotes.

qwen-image-2512.summary: The December 2025 update of Alibaba's open Qwen Image. It made people, nature and text look more real than the first version. Words only: no reference pictures.
good: More natural faces, skin and expressions than the first Qwen Image.
Fine detail in landscapes, animals and buildings.
Readable text built into the picture.
A wide range of shapes, from very wide to tall.
limits: Words only; it can't edit or use reference pictures.
Superseded by Qwen Image 2.1, which adds editing, references and transparent backgrounds.
qwen-image-2512.best_for: Cheap photoreal pictures with simple text, from words only

qwen-image-3.summary: Alibaba's closed Qwen Image 3.0 (July 2026), built for pictures that carry information: posters, infographics, menus, interface mock-ups and storyboards full of small, legible text. It also edits with up to three reference pictures.
good: Dense, legible text and layout in one pass: newspaper pages, infographic grids, product sheets.
Reads very long prompts, so you can describe a whole page area by area.
Text in many languages.
Edits with up to three reference pictures: add labels, swap backgrounds, combine elements.
limits: General picture quality trails the top closed models; choose it for layout, not beauty.
Small print, figures and non-Latin scripts still slip, and chart numbers can be wrong; proof everything.
Slow for a picture model, and only square or near-square shapes.
Edits come out smaller than new pictures.
qwen-image-3.best_for: Infographics, menus, posters and mock-ups packed with readable text
qwen-image-3.tip: Put every piece of copy in quotes and describe the page area by area. Check names, dates and figures; it can invent numbers.

wan-2.2-i2v-flash.summary: A hosted speed tier of Alibaba's 2025 Wan 2.2. It animates a start frame into a short, silent clip for little money. Fine for quick motion tests; Wan 2.7 and 3.0 outclass it.
good: Cheap, quick motion tests from a still.
Keeps the look, subject and layout of the start frame.
Follows simple camera directions such as a slow push-in.
limits: Older generation: lower resolution, short clips, no sound.
You can't set the clip length.
Leave 'things to avoid' empty and Segmind's default steers it away from busy city scenes; type your own to override.
wan-2.2-i2v-flash.best_for: Cheap motion tests of a keyframe

codeformer.summary: CodeFormer, a well-known open face-restoration model from 2022. It rebuilds blurry or damaged faces in old photos or AI pictures, and can enlarge the rest of the picture.
good: Brings blurry, low-quality faces back to sharp eyes, teeth and skin
Works on old scans as well as AI faces
Cheap and quick
limits: Creative on faces: it redraws them, so a real person can end up looking like someone else
Its licence bars commercial use without its makers' permission
Restored faces can look smooth and slightly artificial next to the original grain
codeformer.best_for: Quick fixes for blurry faces in drafts

chroma.summary: Chroma, an open, community-trained model reworked from FLUX.1 schnell. It covers many styles and filters less than most; it's slower than the typical image model here.
good: A wide range of styles, from photo to illustration
Accepts 'things to avoid', which most FLUX-family models don't
Open, permissive licence
Many shapes, from very wide to tall
limits: One of the slower image models here
Built to be uncensored, so it filters less; review results before sharing
Older FLUX.1 base: current flagships follow complex prompts and lettering better

sdxl1.0-txt2img.summary: SDXL 1.0, Stability AI's 2023 open image model and the base that most of the community models in this list are built on. A plain, general-purpose generator; useful as a cheap baseline.
good: Handles photo, illustration, 3D and painting looks reasonably well
Better faces and layout than the older SD 1.5 models
Cheap and fast
Segmind runs a second finishing pass that adds fine detail
limits: Trails today's flagships badly on hands, crowds and following long prompts
Text in the picture is hit and miss beyond a word or two
Square pictures only in the Studio
The community models built on it usually look better for a specific style
sdxl1.0-txt2img.best_for: A cheap, neutral baseline or quick concept sketch

grok-imagine-video.summary: xAI's first Grok Imagine Video: clips with sound from words or a start frame. Replaced by Grok Imagine Video 1.5.
good: Sound in the same pass: ambience, effects, music, dialogue.
A start frame anchors the look; the prompt just drives motion.
Wide choice of lengths and frame shapes.
limits: Older generation: Grok Imagine Video 1.5 is faster and better at motion.
No end frame or reference pictures.
Physics and complex action fall short of the best models.

wan-2.2-i2v-fast.summary: Alibaba's open Wan 2.2 animator, run on Segmind's own servers. One of the cheapest ways to animate a start frame, and it can aim for an end frame too. Clips are short, silent and lower resolution.
good: Among the cheapest picture-to-clip models here.
Takes a start and an end frame, so it can link two Board keyframes on a budget.
Fluid motion for its age; Wan 2.2 learned from much more video than 2.1.
limits: Clips are about five seconds and lower resolution.
Landscape or tall only; no square.
No sound.
Older generation: motion and detail trail Wan 2.7 and 3.0.
wan-2.2-i2v-fast.best_for: Budget moves between a start and an end keyframe

flux-1.1-pro-ultra.summary: The 'Ultra' version of FLUX 1.1 Pro (late 2024): larger, more detailed pictures without a big speed penalty. Known for a Raw mode that gives a candid, less polished photo look.
good: Bigger, more detailed pictures than FLUX 1.1 Pro.
Strong prompt-following for its generation.
Quick for its size.
Wide choice of shapes, including tall and wide banners.
limits: The Studio doesn't switch on Raw mode, the natural candid look it's best known for.
Its one reference picture is loose inspiration only.
Two generations behind FLUX 3.
flux-1.1-pro-ultra.best_for: Larger photoreal pictures from the FLUX.1 era

flux-kontext-dev.summary: The open, cheapest tier of FLUX.1 Kontext (mid-2025): edits one picture from a plain instruction. It needs a picture to work on.
good: Edits from a plain sentence: restyle, recolour, change the background.
Keeps a character recognisable over a few edits.
Cheap and quick.
limits: Lower quality than Kontext Pro and Max.
Older generation: FLUX 3 Klein edits for less money with more control.
One picture only.

sdxl1.0-newreality-lightning.summary: NewReality in a fast version: a community SDXL model that aims for photo realism with a creative, slightly stylised twist.
good: Realistic-looking pictures with some imaginative flair
Fast and cheap
Takes an 'avoid' list and a seed
limits: Older SDXL generation: hands, text and complex prompts trail today's models
Square pictures only
The speed shortcut costs some detail and variety
sdxl1.0-newreality-lightning.best_for: Fast photo-ish concept frames with a creative edge

gpt-image-1-mini.summary: A cheaper, lighter GPT Image 1, words-to-picture only here, with transparent-background output. Fine for cheap drafts; overtaken by the newer GPT Image models.
good: One of the cheaper OpenAI image options.
Transparent backgrounds for simple cut-outs.
Decent prompt following.
limits: Lower quality than full GPT Image 1, let alone GPT Image 2.5.
Takes no reference pictures in this version.
Only three frame shapes and a modest top size.
gpt-image-1-mini.best_for: Cheap drafts with a simple cut-out

hailuo-2.3-fast.summary: The faster, cheaper version of Hailuo 2.3. It only animates a start frame you supply and can't make a clip from words alone. Silent.
good: Quick and cheap: a fast way to bring a Board keyframe to life.
Keeps Hailuo 2.3's natural movement and facial expressions.
The clip takes the shape of your start frame, so the framing stays as you composed it.
limits: Needs a start frame. It can't work from words alone.
No sound and no end frame.
Clips are 6 or 10 seconds only, and 10 seconds only at the lower resolution.
Gives up some quality for speed compared with full Hailuo 2.3.
hailuo-2.3-fast.best_for: Fast, cheap animation of a keyframe still

stable-diffusion-3.5-turbo-txt2img.summary: The fast version of Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, Stability AI's late-2024 open model, trained to finish in a few steps. Follows prompts and handles short text better than the SDXL models here, at a low price.
good: Follows multi-part prompts better than the SDXL and SD 1.5 models in this list
Puts a short word or headline into the picture more often than older SD models
Wide range of looks: photo, 3D, painting, line art
Cheap and quick
limits: Two years old: hands, small faces and fine detail trail FLUX-class and newer models
Text works for a word or two, not for longer copy
Less detail than the full SD 3.5 Large
Your 'avoid' list does little at the fast settings it runs with
stable-diffusion-3.5-turbo-txt2img.best_for: Cheap drafts that need the prompt followed, or a short word in frame
stable-diffusion-3.5-turbo-txt2img.tip: Put any words you want shown in quotation marks and keep them short.

wan2.6-i2v-flash.summary: The quick tier of Wan 2.6 (late 2025). It animates a start frame into a clip with a matching soundtrack, cheaply. A good budget choice when you want sound.
good: Makes sound with the picture: effects, ambience, and speech with matching mouths.
Cheap for a clip with sound.
Lengths from a couple of seconds up to fifteen.
Keeps the lighting, layout and subject of the start frame.
limits: Needs a start frame; it can't write a clip from words alone.
No end frame and no reference pictures.
Faces, hands, text and logos can shift as things move.
Older than Wan 2.7 and 3.0.
wan2.6-i2v-flash.best_for: Cheap clips with sound from a single still
wan2.6-i2v-flash.tip: Start from a sharp, well-lit still; it amplifies whatever you feed it. Turn sound off when you don't need it; the clip costs less.

kling-2.6-standard-motion-control.summary: Kling 2.6 motion transfer, Standard tier: copies the movement from a clip you supply onto the person or character in a still. A dance, gesture or walk, performed by someone new.
good: Copies full-body movement, including hands and facial expression, from a real performance
Works on photos and on illustrated or 3D characters with a human-like body
Can keep the reference clip's own sound, useful for dance or speech timing
You choose whether the character faces as in the picture or follows the clip's facing
limits: Needs both a motion clip and a picture; it doesn't invent movement from words
Motion clips are capped at 10 seconds when facing follows the picture, 30 when it follows the clip
Works best with one clearly visible, full-body performer; crowds or cropped bodies transfer poorly
Slow: several minutes per clip
kling-2.6-standard-motion-control.best_for: Making a still character perform a real person's moves
kling-2.6-standard-motion-control.tip: Film the move on a phone: one person, whole body in frame, plain background, good light. Use a picture with similar framing and pose.

p-video-2.summary: Pruna's own second-generation video model. It makes clips with sound, up to full HD, from words, a start frame, or a start and end frame. Fast and cheap for what you get.
good: Sound made with the picture: speech, music and effects
Full HD and longer clips than most fast models
Start and end frames to control where a shot begins and lands
Quick, and one of the cheaper clips with sound
limits: Clips come with sound by default even though the Studio shows no sound switch
Built for speed and price: expect less polish than the flagship video models
With a start frame, the frame sets the shape and the aspect setting is ignored
Its option to drive a clip from your own voice-over isn't available in the Studio
p-video-2.best_for: Fast, cheap full-HD clips with sound
p-video-2.tip: Put spoken lines in quotes and name the sounds: She says: 'Ready?' Rain patters on the awning. For a start frame, describe the motion, not the scene.

flux-img2img.summary: FLUX.1 Dev's image-to-image mode: it repaints your picture in a new style or look while roughly keeping its composition.
good: Restyles a photo while keeping its broad layout.
Can turn a rough sketch or snapshot into a finished-looking image.
Has a seed for repeatable results.
limits: One of the slowest stills here.
It repaints the whole picture, so faces, logos and small details drift; it can't make a targeted edit.
Older generation: FLUX 3 Klein edits are faster and precise.
flux-img2img.best_for: Loose restyles of a sketch or photo

sdxl1.0-realdream-pony-v9.summary: Real Dream Pony, a realistic community model by the creator 'sinatra', built on Pony, an SDXL model from the fan-art world. Aims for lifelike skin and lighting.
good: Lifelike lighting and skin for an SDXL-era model
Best at single-person portraits
Takes an 'avoid' list and a seed
limits: Pony-based models lean toward glamour and adult content: keep an 'avoid' list on and check every take
Older SDXL generation: hands and text are unreliable
Square pictures only in the Studio
Pony models expect special quality tags (score_9 and similar) to look their best
sdxl1.0-realdream-pony-v9.best_for: Realistic single portraits, when you want this particular look
sdxl1.0-realdream-pony-v9.tip: Starting the prompt with 'score_9, score_8_up,' is the usual way to get the polished look Pony models are tuned for.

clarityai-flux-upscaler.summary: Clarity AI's creative upscaler built on FLUX. It enlarges the picture and adds new detail, steered by the prompt, and by default it invents a moderate amount.
good: Rebuilds texture and fine detail on soft or small pictures
The Studio passes the take's own prompt, so the new detail fits the scene
A newer engine than the original Clarity Upscaler
limits: Creative: it invents detail, so faces, hands and small lettering can change
One of the slowest and priciest picture upscalers here
Not for product shots or real people who must stay exact
clarityai-flux-upscaler.best_for: Adding believable detail to soft AI pictures
clarityai-flux-upscaler.tip: Check faces and lettering against the original before using it. For a straight, faithful enlargement use Crystal.

flux-kontext-pro.summary: The standard tier of FLUX.1 Kontext (mid-2025): edits a picture from a plain instruction, or makes one from words. It sits between the open Dev and the top Max tier.
good: Instruction edits: change the background, clothes, colour or time of day.
Keeps a person's likeness across edits better than older repaint tools.
Quick and moderately priced.
Works with or without a picture.
limits: Takes one reference picture.
Weaker at type than Kontext Max.
Quality can drift after many edits in a row.
Superseded by FLUX 3's edit mode.
flux-kontext-pro.best_for: Everyday one-picture edits from a sentence
flux-kontext-pro.tip: Say what must stay as well as what changes: 'swap the background for a minimalist office, keep her face and pose'.

kling-2.6-pro-motion-control.summary: Kling 2.6 motion transfer, Pro tier: puts the movement from your clip onto the character in a still, with more care over detail than Standard. Your prompt sets the look and mood; the motion comes from the clip.
good: Copies full-body movement, including hands and facial expression, from a real performance
Handles fast, complex moves such as dance routines and martial arts
Works on photos and on illustrated or 3D characters with a human-like body
Can keep the reference clip's own sound
limits: Needs both a motion clip and a picture; it doesn't invent movement from words
Motion clips are capped at 10 seconds when facing follows the picture, 30 when it follows the clip
Works best with one clearly visible, full-body performer; crowds or cropped bodies transfer poorly
Slow: several minutes per clip, slower than Standard
kling-2.6-pro-motion-control.best_for: Final renders of a real performance copied onto a new character
kling-2.6-pro-motion-control.tip: Check the transfer in Standard first, then render the keeper in Pro. For intricate hand work, use a short, slow reference clip.

qwen-image-edit-plus-blend-it.summary: Qwen Image Edit 2509 with a small add-on (a LoRA: extra training that teaches one skill) for dropping a product or object into a background picture and matching the light and perspective.
good: Matches lighting, shadows and perspective when placing a product into a new scene.
Takes up to three pictures: the subject, the background and one extra element.
Cheap and quick for composite drafts.
limits: Built on the 2025 editor; Qwen Image 2.1 does product-in-scene composites with more reference pictures.
It doesn't keep your photo's shape by itself; choose the shape you want.
qwen-image-edit-plus-blend-it.best_for: Placing a product photo into a background picture
qwen-image-edit-plus-blend-it.tip: Attach the product first and the background second, and describe the light: 'set the bottle on the counter with soft window light and a matching shadow'.

stable-diffusion-3.5-large-txt2img.summary: Stable Diffusion 3.5 Large, Stability AI's flagship open image model from late 2024. The best prompt follower of the Stability models here, with a wide range of styles, but well behind today's leaders on detail and hands.
good: Follows longer, multi-part prompts better than any other Stability model in the Studio
Handles many looks: photo, illustration, 3D, painting
Renders a short word, like a sign or a label, more reliably than SDXL
Takes an 'avoid' list and a seed
limits: Community tests generally put FLUX-class models ahead on looks and realism; today's flagships are further ahead
Hands and anatomy still slip, especially in busy scenes
Longer text in the picture still breaks
Slower than the Turbo and Lightning models here
stable-diffusion-3.5-large-txt2img.best_for: An open-model look with decent prompt following at a modest price
stable-diffusion-3.5-large-txt2img.tip: Describe the scene in plain sentences rather than keyword lists; SD 3.5 reads full sentences better than the older SD models.

sdxl1.0-samaritan-3d.summary: Samaritan 3D, a community SDXL model for cute, expressive cartoon characters in a 3D animated-film style.
good: Cute, rounded 3D cartoon characters with clear expressions
Consistent animated-film look without long style prompts
Takes an 'avoid' list and a seed
limits: One look only: not for photos or flat illustration
Older SDXL generation: hands, text and scenes with several characters are weak
Square pictures only
Takes no reference picture, so the same character won't hold across takes
sdxl1.0-samaritan-3d.best_for: 3D cartoon mascots and characters for mockups

kling-2.5-turbo.summary: Kling 2.5 Turbo, a lower-cost Kling from late 2025. Writes a clip from words or animates a still, and can end on an end frame. Silent.
good: Fluid, natural motion; handles dance and sports moves well for its age
Follows detailed prompts and camera directions
Start frame and end frame, for clips that must land on a keyframe
Costs less than the Kling 3.0 tiers
limits: No sound
Clips are 5 or 10 seconds only
The end frame only works together with a start frame, and a start frame's shape overrides the aspect setting
Slow in practice despite the name: a few minutes per clip
kling-2.5-turbo.best_for: Silent shots and keyframe-to-keyframe moves on a budget

ideogram-3.summary: Ideogram 3.0 (March 2025), the version that cemented Ideogram as the go-to for text in pictures, with better photorealism than before. Cheap and quick; now overtaken by Ideogram 4.x.
good: Reliably spelled text for posters, flyers and logos.
Wide choice of shapes, including very tall and very wide banners.
Accepts a 'things to avoid' prompt.
Cheap and quick.
limits: Web-size output only.
Older generation than Ideogram 4.5.
No reference pictures in the Studio, so no brand style or product.
ideogram-3.best_for: Cheap text-led graphics in unusual banner shapes

p-video-2-pro-reference.summary: Pruna's reference-to-video model, built on MiniMax's H3. Its job is keeping a person or product consistent from clip to clip, with sound. In the Studio it works from a start frame and an optional end frame.
good: Sound made with every clip
Its maker reports faces and clothing carried over well from a reference picture
Start and end frames give frame-exact openings and endings
Inexpensive for a clip with sound
limits: Words alone are refused: it needs at least one picture, so always give it a start frame
The Studio passes only start and end frames, not the extra reference pictures (cast, products) its maker describes
Top resolution is lower than most video models here
References are loose guides: anything the prompt doesn't name can be dropped
p-video-2-pro-reference.best_for: Animating a still of a person or product, with sound
p-video-2-pro-reference.tip: Always attach a start frame. In the prompt, say what the picture should contribute, and keep to one action and one sound.

gemini-omni-flash.summary: Google's first Gemini Omni video model (Omni Flash, 2026). Clips with sound from words, up to 14 reference pictures, or a reference video to restyle (beta). Replaced by Gemini Omni 1.1.
good: Strong physics and environments; objects react to each other believably.
Sound with the picture, with natural-sounding voices and timing.
Reference pictures anchor a character or product.
Timecodes in the prompt land precisely.
limits: Refuses real people: won't work from a real person's photo or likeness. The Studio marks it 'no real people'.
Mouths stop matching the speech after the first several seconds, and lines get mixed up between people.
Won't stage fights or rough physical contact between people.
No start or end frame; the reference-video mode is beta and may fail.
gemini-omni-flash.best_for: Short clips with sound built from reference pictures

minimax-h3-reference-to-video.summary: The H3 mode for keeping a subject the same. Give it a few reference pictures of a person or product, describe the action, and it builds a new, very sharp scene around them.
good: Holds a face, outfit or product steady from the first frame to the last.
Puts your subject into a new scene rather than just animating the reference picture.
Very sharp output, above full HD.
Good for product spots and recurring characters across a set of shots.
limits: One of the slowest models here. Expect a long wait for every take.
Can't start or end on a frame you choose. The framing comes from the prompt.
Sound can't be switched on or steered here.
Takes fewer reference pictures than H3 Max Reference.
minimax-h3-reference-to-video.best_for: Keeping a person or product identical in a sharp new scene
minimax-h3-reference-to-video.tip: Give each picture one job (front face, three-quarter, full body). In the prompt, name the traits that must hold: hair, jacket colour, which way the label faces.

p-video-replace.summary: Pruna's person swap for footage, built on Lightricks' LTX-2. It replaces the person in your clip with the person in your pictures, keeping the motion, camera move, background and original sound.
good: Swaps the whole person, posture and movement included, not just the face
Keeps your clip's camera move, lighting, setting and sound
Takes up to three pictures of the new person for a steadier likeness
One good clip can be recast many times
limits: People only: it takes no instruction, so it can't swap products or clothes
The likeness can drift when the head turns away or the camera whips round
In a shot with several people you can't choose who gets replaced
p-video-replace.best_for: Recasting the person in a clip you already have
p-video-replace.tip: Use clean, front-facing, well-lit portraits of the new person, plus a side view if they turn. Make sure you hold that person's release.

flux-krea-dev.summary: FLUX.1 Krea, an open model Krea trained with Black Forest Labs to avoid the 'AI look': fewer fake-blurred backgrounds, plastic skin and over-cooked colour. Good for natural-looking photos.
good: A more natural, photographic look than stock FLUX.1 Dev.
Fewer over-smoothed faces and fake-blurred backgrounds.
Cheap and quick.
Can rework a starting picture you supply.
limits: First-generation FLUX underneath: weaker text and prompt-following than FLUX 3.
Its starting picture is repainted loosely, not edited precisely.
Modest output size; not for big print crops.
flux-krea-dev.best_for: Natural, un-glossy photo looks on a budget

minimax-h3-max-reference-to-video.summary: fal's fast, tuned H3 for reference pictures. A full kit of pictures pins a person or product, and the prompt sets the action and scene. Much quicker than plain H3 Reference, at lower resolution.
good: Holds identity through fast motion: spins, orbits, a product turning on a table.
Takes more reference pictures than plain H3 Reference. Several angles tighten the likeness.
Quick for a reference model, usually about a minute or less.
Works for people and products alike.
limits: Below full HD. For sharp delivery, use H3 Reference to Video.
Every reference picture after the first two adds to the cost, so a big kit costs more than the average shown.
No start or end frame, and no sound.
minimax-h3-max-reference-to-video.best_for: Fast, consistent kit shots of a product or character
minimax-h3-max-reference-to-video.tip: Let the pictures carry the look and keep appearance out of the prompt; write only action, camera and setting. References on plain backgrounds give the cleanest lock.

qwen-image-edit.summary: Alibaba's first Qwen editor (August 2025). It changes a picture by instruction, including rewriting the text in it while keeping the font. Slow and pricey for its age; newer Qwen editors do more.
good: Rewrites text inside a picture, in English or Chinese, keeping the original font, size and style.
Handles both big changes (style, weather, moving things) and small local fixes.
Can turn an object or change its colour or texture by instruction.
limits: Slow and one of the pricier editors here, for older results.
Works on one picture; no extra reference pictures.
Superseded by Qwen Image Edit Plus and Qwen Image 2.1.
qwen-image-edit.best_for: Swapping the words on a sign or label while keeping the lettering style

qwen-image-edit-fast.summary: A quick, cheap run of the first Qwen editor (August 2025). Good at swapping the text on signs and labels and making simple changes to one picture.
good: Quick and cheap.
Replaces text on signs and packaging, in English or Chinese, keeping the font and style.
Makes small, targeted changes without disturbing the rest of the picture.
limits: One picture only.
Older generation: Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo is newer, cheaper and takes ten reference pictures.
qwen-image-edit-fast.best_for: Quick text swaps on signs and labels
qwen-image-edit-fast.tip: Name the exact words: 'replace the sign text with "Open Late"' works better than 'change the sign'.

qwen-image-fast.summary: A quick, cheap run of the first Qwen Image (August 2025), known for putting readable text, Chinese included, into pictures. Words only.
good: Very quick and cheap.
Readable text in pictures, especially Chinese characters.
Handles photoreal and illustrated styles in many shapes.
limits: Words only; no editing or reference pictures.
First-generation Qwen: newer Qwen and Z-Image models look better for similar money.
qwen-image-fast.best_for: Cheap drafts with simple text in them

seedance-2.5-upscaled.summary: Seedance 2.5 with a different finish. It renders one size smaller, then enlarges the clip with an AI upscaler, so you can get full HD or 4K delivery. You keep the same long takes, sound and kit references as Seedance 2.5.
good: The way to get a Seedance 2.5 shot at 4K.
Everything Seedance 2.5 does: long takes, several shots per clip, sound, kit references, start and end frames.
Suits hero shots where the finished clip has to hold up on a big screen.
limits: Enlarged rather than rendered at full size, so fine texture is filled in by the upscaler and can look sharp but not quite real.
The slowest and most expensive Seedance here.
Same rules as Seedance 2.5: no real faces in a start frame, and a refusal can arrive after the full wait.
seedance-2.5-upscaled.tip: Settle the shot on plain Seedance 2.5 at a small size first, then run the final here. The same prompt and seed should land close, but it isn't guaranteed.

gpt-image-1-edit.summary: The edit version of GPT Image 1: attach pictures and describe the change. It swaps objects, skies, labels or backgrounds and combines several pictures into one. Overtaken by GPT Image 2.5.
good: Combines several product pictures into one composed shot, e.g. items into a gift basket.
Swaps a sky, a label or a background from a plain instruction.
Transparent output for cut-outs.
limits: Older generation: less precise at leaving untouched areas alone than GPT Image 2.5.
Slow, and one of the dearest edit models here.
Needs at least one picture; only three frame shapes.
gpt-image-1-edit.best_for: Rarely: GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst does careful edits better

bria-fibo-image-edit.summary: Bria's newest editor (FIBO 2.0), trained on licensed images only. Describe the change in plain words; it can also combine your picture with reference pictures, e.g. put a product into a new scene.
good: Keeps a product's shape and label while the scene around it changes
Takes up to four pictures: the one to edit plus references
Licensed-data training, a plus for commercial use
Independent tests rate it well for clean-up, restoration and scene or style changes
limits: Lettering and layout changes are its weakest area in independent tests
Composition changes and multi-step edits lag the leading editors
Its 'things to avoid' box has no effect on this version
bria-fibo-image-edit.best_for: Licensed-safe product edits and scene swaps
bria-fibo-image-edit.tip: Add 'keep the product unchanged' to the instruction to lock its shape and label. Keep the seed to repeat an edit exactly.

grok-imagine-video-1.5-reference-to-vide.summary: Grok Imagine Video 1.5 steered by up to seven reference pictures instead of a start frame. It keeps a person, product or outfit consistent while you change the action, setting and camera. Sound included.
good: Holds a face, outfit and props through a clip from even one clean reference picture.
References don't lock the first frame, so you can put the subject anywhere.
Mix a character and a product in one shot.
Sound in the same pass.
limits: Lower top size than plain Grok Imagine Video 1.5.
No start or end frame.
Reviewers found continuity breaks across multi-shot scenes and weak action physics.
grok-imagine-video-1.5-reference-to-vide.best_for: Keeping a kit character or product consistent across shots
grok-imagine-video-1.5-reference-to-vide.tip: Use clean, well-lit reference pictures on plain backgrounds, and spend the prompt on action, camera and sound rather than describing the subject.

qwen-image.summary: Alibaba's first Qwen Image (August 2025), the open model that brought long, accurate text in pictures to everyone. Words only, and now outclassed by its successors.
good: Accurate text, from single words to whole paragraphs, in English and Chinese.
Good prompt following for its time.
Many shapes, from square to wide.
limits: Dearer than its newer, better siblings.
Words only; it can't edit or use reference pictures.
Segmind's default 'avoid' list includes 'cartoonish'; for cartoon or illustration styles, fill in your own.
qwen-image.best_for: Posters with paragraph-length text, if newer Qwen models aren't an option

sdxl1.0-dreamshaper-lightning.summary: The fast version of DreamShaper XL by the community creator Lykon: a general-purpose SDXL model that does photos, painterly art, anime and fantasy.
good: One model for photos, painterly art, anime and fantasy
Fast and cheap
Good at fantasy and concept-art moods
limits: Older SDXL generation: hands, text and complex prompts trail today's models
Square pictures only
A jack of all trades: the photo-realism models here beat it at plain photos

kolors.summary: An open image model Kuaishou released in 2024, separate from the Kling line. Writes a picture from words, quickly and very cheaply. Its main distinction is understanding Chinese prompts.
good: Very quick and one of the cheapest images here, good for rough ideas
Understands prompts in Chinese as well as English
Pleasant color and light for illustration and simple scenes
Better than most 2024 open models at short Chinese text
limits: 2024 generation: hands, crowds and fine detail fall well short of current models
Unreliable at English text in pictures
No reference pictures and no frame-shape choice in the Studio
kolors.best_for: Fast, cheap rough ideas, or prompts written in Chinese

qwen-image-edit-plus-multiple-angle.summary: Qwen Image Edit 2509 with an add-on that moves the camera: describe a new viewpoint and it redraws the same scene or product from there. Useful for extra angles of a product shot or keyframe.
good: Turns, raises or pulls back the camera by instruction: front, side and three-quarter views from one photo.
Switches between wide and close framing of the same scene.
Gives the Board a second angle on a keyframe, so cuts feel shot on one set.
Works on photos, illustrations and 3D renders.
limits: It has to invent what the original camera never saw, so the hidden side of a product may be wrong.
Built on the 2025 editor, so fine detail trails newer models.
It doesn't keep your photo's shape by itself; pick the shape.
qwen-image-edit-plus-multiple-angle.best_for: A second camera angle of a product or keyframe
qwen-image-edit-plus-multiple-angle.tip: Give a concrete move: 'rotate the camera 45 degrees to the left' or 'move the camera back and up to show the whole facade'.

sdxl1.0-realvis-lightning.summary: The fast version of RealVisXL by SG_161222 (the maker of Realistic Vision), an SDXL photo-realism model focused on believable people.
good: Photo-style people with natural skin and hair for an SDXL model
Good for lifestyle and portrait drafts
Takes an 'avoid' list and a seed
limits: Older SDXL generation: hands, groups and text trail today's models
Square pictures only
Here it's no quicker or cheaper than the full RealVis SDXL, which has a bit more detail

veo-3.summary: Google's Veo 3 (2025): clips with sound from words or a start frame. Replaced by Veo 3.1, which adds end frames and reference pictures.
good: Sound with the picture, including dialogue with matching mouths.
Good physics and film-language control.
More frame shapes than Veo 3.1, including square and 4:3.
limits: Refuses real people: won't work from a real person's photo or likeness. The Studio marks it 'no real people'.
No end frame or reference pictures.
Superseded by Veo 3.1 on quality and control.

flux-pro.summary: FLUX.1 Pro (August 2024), the original paid top tier of FLUX. Replaced by FLUX 1.1 Pro within months and now several steps behind FLUX 3.
good: Good prompt-following and detail for its time.
Quick.
Varied results from the same prompt.
limits: Superseded twice over; FLUX 1.1 Pro was already faster and better.
No reference pictures.
Costs more than newer, better models such as FLUX 3 Klein.
flux-pro.best_for: Matching the look of older FLUX.1 Pro work

happyhorse.summary: The first HappyHorse (April 2026), which topped a public blind-vote video leaderboard at launch. It makes picture and sound together, and unlike 1.1 it can end on a set frame and work on an existing clip.
good: Start frame and end frame, so it can link two Board keyframes.
Can take an existing clip and restyle or change it, as a Change option.
Picture and sound made together; mouths match the speech in seven languages.
Strong nature and documentary-style footage: smooth motion, warm light, shallow focus.
Led a public blind-vote leaderboard for both words-to-clip and picture-to-clip at launch.
limits: Replaced by 1.1, which improves motion, consistency and detail.
One of the pricier clips here.
Short clips: fifteen seconds at most.
happyhorse.best_for: Linking two keyframes with sound, or restyling a short clip

recraft-v4-svg.summary: Recraft V4's vector version: it returns a real, editable SVG file (paths and layers) instead of pixels. For logos, icons and flat illustrations you'll scale or edit in Illustrator or Figma.
good: A true vector file: scales from favicon to billboard and opens as editable paths in Illustrator, Figma or Sketch.
Draws in shapes rather than tracing a bitmap, so outlines come out clean.
Can return a whole icon set in one file with matching line weight.
Legible titles and labels as part of the design.
Up to ten style pictures keep it on-brand.
limits: Flat shapes only: the wrong tool for photos, grain, texture or soft gradients.
The Studio can't set its shape; Recraft picks one from your prompt.
Style pictures copy a look, not a specific logo or product.
Busy scenes get simplified; the Pro SVG tier keeps finer detail.
recraft-v4-svg.best_for: Logos, icons and flat illustrations you'll edit or scale
recraft-v4-svg.tip: Name every element and quote the text. Say the shape in words ('square icon sheet', 'wide hero illustration'), and ask for 'flat colour' to keep it clean.

bria-fibo-generate.summary: Bria's newest text-to-image model (FIBO 2.0), trained only on licensed images. It first expands your prompt into a detailed scene description, which gives precise, repeatable control of light, camera and placement.
good: Photoreal portraits and products with fine detail
Follows object placement well, e.g. 'the second apple from the left is a pear'
Licensed-data training: a strong choice where legal clarity matters
You can change one thing (light, lens) without the rest of the scene drifting
limits: Words inside the picture and layout are its weakest area in independent tests
Composition and framing lag the top commercial models
Takes no reference pictures in the Studio
bria-fibo-generate.tip: Describe light, lens and mood plainly; it fills in the rest. Keep the seed to rerun a shot with one change.

hailuo-02-fast.summary: A cheap, quick version of Hailuo 02, from mid-2025. It animates a start frame, optionally toward an end frame, at low resolution. For rough motion tests.
good: A cheap way to test motion from a still.
Takes both a start and an end frame, which Hailuo 2.3 doesn't.
Hailuo 02's physics were strong for their time: water, splashes, gymnastics.
limits: Low resolution, below HD. Drafts only.
Needs a start frame, so no clips from words alone.
No sound, and clips are 6 or 10 seconds only.
Old generation. H3 Max Turbo is the better quick option now.
hailuo-02-fast.best_for: Rough start-to-end motion tests on a tight budget

kling-o3-video2video-reference.summary: Kling O3's reference mode for footage: takes your clip as a guide for movement and camera, and makes a new version that brings in a person, product or look from reference pictures.
good: Brings kit pictures (a person, a product, a style) into a new version of your shot
Follows the source clip's movement and camera
Several reference pictures at once, e.g. a character plus a style
Can keep the source clip's original sound
limits: The slowest Kling edit here: several minutes per clip
One of the most expensive edits in the Studio
The source clip must be at least 720 pixels wide
Makes no new sound
kling-o3-video2video-reference.best_for: Recasting or restyling a shot from kit pictures while keeping its movement
kling-o3-video2video-reference.tip: Call pictures @Image1, @Image2 in the order attached. Keep the stretch of clip to 10 seconds or less. For a single swap, try O3 Video Edit first.

fooocus.summary: Fooocus, a popular open SDXL app from the maker of ControlNet, built to give polished results from a short prompt. An older generation, here for its look.
good: Good-looking SDXL results from short prompts; it expands the prompt for you
Accepts 'things to avoid'
A familiar SDXL look, if that's what you want
limits: Old SDXL generation: weak hands, poor lettering, misses parts of complex prompts
No seed, so you can't repeat a result
Costs more than newer, fast models that beat it
fooocus.best_for: An SDXL-style look, when you specifically want one

recraft-v3.summary: Recraft V3 (late 2024), the model that put Recraft on the map: it topped public leaderboards at launch and handled longer text than its rivals. Design-minded pictures; now replaced by V4.
good: Clean design sense for posters, flyers and social graphics.
Legible text, including longer lines than most models of its time.
Very quick.
limits: No reference pictures or seed in the Studio.
Recraft V4 has better layout, colour and detail.
Recraft's preset styles (pixel art, hand-drawn and so on) aren't selectable in the Studio.
recraft-v3.best_for: Fast, text-led design graphics on a budget

veed-video-background-removal.summary: VEED's video background remover. No prompt: give it a clip and it cuts out the person or object without a green screen. It also keys real green-screen footage and cleans up the green spill.
good: Cuts people out of ordinary, cluttered or moving backgrounds; no green screen needed.
Edge refinement keeps hair and fine outlines clean.
Green-screen mode cleans up footage shot on a green screen, including the green fringe.
limits: Tuned for people by default; products and objects need a different setting.
Dim, low-contrast or busy footage gives rougher edges.
Gives you a cut-out, not a new background; you layer it over a new background elsewhere.
veed-video-background-removal.best_for: Cutting a presenter out of footage to place on a new background

kling-2.6.summary: Kling 2.6 in Pro mode: animates a still, or writes a clip from words, with sound made alongside. The generation before Kling 3.0.
good: Makes sound with the picture: ambience, effects and voices
Smooth camera moves and steady scenes from a single still
Costs less than Kling 3.0 Pro
Takes a 'things to avoid' list
limits: Clips are 5 or 10 seconds only
No end frame, so it can't land on a second keyframe
Slow: a few minutes per clip
Previous generation: Kling 3.0 Pro adds an end frame and finer control of length
kling-2.6.best_for: Kling clips with sound on a smaller budget

kling-o1-video-to-video-edit.summary: The first Change tool in Kling's Omni line: edits an existing clip from a written instruction, such as swapping the background or replacing an object, with reference pictures as a guide. Replaced by O3 Video Edit.
good: Edits from words, with no need to mark areas by hand
Keeps the clip's movement while swapping background, objects or props
Takes reference pictures for what to put in
Quicker and cheaper than O3 Video Edit
limits: Previous Omni generation; O3 Video Edit is the newer version
Makes no new sound
Output length follows the source clip; there's no duration choice
kling-o1-video-to-video-edit.best_for: A cheaper, quicker first try at a Change before using O3
kling-o1-video-to-video-edit.tip: Call attached pictures @Image1, @Image2 in the order attached, and say what must stay the same.

p-video-edit.summary: Pruna's editor for your own footage. Describe one change (outfit, product, sky, setting or style) and it redoes the clip while keeping the original motion, framing and sound.
good: Keeps the performance, camera move and timing; only what you name changes
Up to four reference pictures to match an exact garment or product
Keeps the original soundtrack
A good fit for the Studio's Change tool
limits: Source clips can be up to 15 seconds
Slow: a few minutes a clip
Works best with one explicit change per run; vague or stacked instructions go astray
p-video-edit.best_for: Changing wardrobe, product or setting in real footage
p-video-edit.tip: Name what changes and what stays: 'replace the white t-shirt with the jacket in the picture, keep her pose and the studio background'.

wan-2.2-t2v-fast.summary: Alibaba's open Wan 2.2 words-to-clip model, run on Segmind's own servers. The cheapest way here to turn a prompt into a short, silent, lower-resolution clip.
good: One of the cheapest words-to-clip models in the Studio.
Decent motion and camera moves for its age, with good control of light and colour tone.
Landscape or tall output for web and social drafts.
limits: Clips are about five seconds and lower resolution.
No start frame, reference pictures or sound.
Landscape or tall only.
Older generation: detail and physics trail Wan 2.7 and 3.0.

higgsfield-text2image-soul.summary: Higgsfield's original Soul image model: realistic, phone-camera-style photos with a catalogue of 70+ preset styles and one optional reference picture. Replaced by Soul 2.0.
good: Realistic, un-glossy photo look.
A large catalogue of preset styles.
One reference picture can anchor a style.
Has a seed.
limits: Superseded by Soul 2.0, which adds fashion and editorial fluency.
Styles are picked from coded presets, so you get the default style unless one is set.
Text and fine detail are weaker than the current flagships.

recraft-v4-pro-svg.summary: The high-detail tier of Recraft V4 SVG: editable vector files with finer paths and more geometric detail, for large-format print, detailed illustration and design-system pieces.
good: Finer paths and cleaner geometry than standard V4 SVG.
Real editable vectors: recolour, nudge a corner or reuse a shape without regenerating.
Legible titles and labels built into the layout.
Up to ten style pictures hold a brand look.
limits: Among the priciest stills here; try V4 SVG first.
Flat vector look only: no photos, grain or soft gradients.
The Studio can't set its shape; Recraft picks one from your prompt.
Style pictures copy a look, not your actual logo.
recraft-v4-pro-svg.best_for: Detailed vector illustrations and logos for large print
recraft-v4-pro-svg.tip: Keep quoted text short so it stays crisp, and say the shape in words. Ask for a white background for clean icon sheets.

seedance-pro.summary: The first Seedance Pro, from mid-2025. It makes silent clips from words or a start frame and was good at multi-angle storytelling for its time. The 2.x models add sound and references at a similar price.
good: Clean, steady motion and good prompt following for an older model.
Can cut between camera angles within one clip and keep the scene consistent.
Start and end frames supported.
Handles many looks, from photoreal to illustration.
limits: No sound.
Clips are 5 or 10 seconds only.
No reference pictures.
Costs about the same as Seedance 2.0 Fast, which adds sound and references.
seedance-pro.best_for: Silent multi-angle clips, if a newer Seedance won't do

sam3-video.summary: Meta's Segment Anything 3 for video. It finds and follows the things you name through a clip and returns masks or a coloured overlay, not an edited video.
good: Tracks a named thing ('red sedan', 'man with a baseball cap') through a clip.
Copes with long clips, up to several minutes.
Can follow several objects at once.
limits: Output is masks or an overlay; you still need an editor to use them.
Vague words, low light or heavy compression reduce accuracy.
sam3-video.best_for: Outlining a moving object to treat or replace it separately

bria-remove-background-guided.summary: Bria's background remover that you can talk to. Leave the prompt blank for a normal cutout, or say what to keep or drop ('only the chair', 'the dog without the lead'). Trained on licensed images.
good: Fixes the cases a one-click remover gets wrong
Repaints nothing: it only adds transparency, so colours and detail stay exact
Soft, clean edges on hair and fur
Licensed-data training
limits: Instructions work in English only
Slower and dearer than the one-click remover
Very small pictures and glass reflections are the hardest cases
bria-remove-background-guided.best_for: Cutting one item out of a busy scene
bria-remove-background-guided.tip: Name the target by colour and type ('the red accordion'). Use 'only the...' to narrow the cut and '...without the...' to drop something.

heygen-generate-look.summary: HeyGen's avatar look maker. First you train an identity from about ten photos of one person; then you dress that person in new outfits, settings, poses and styles from words. Built for HeyGen's talking-avatar workflow.
good: Same face across every look once the identity is trained.
Outfit, setting, pose and style (realistic, cinematic, noir and more) from words.
Framing presets: close-up, half body, full body.
limits: Two steps: photos start a training job of 15 to 30 minutes that returns an ID; looks need a second run with that ID.
Training needs about ten clear, varied photos of one person; group shots, hats and sunglasses hurt.
Expensive per run compared with general image models.
heygen-generate-look.best_for: One presenter's headshots in many outfits and settings

kling-o1.summary: Kling's first Omni image model. It makes a still by combining reference pictures with your instruction, such as putting a person into a setting, or from words alone. Segmind's page calls it a video model; here it makes stills.
good: Combines several reference pictures in one image: a person, a product and a place
Follows plain instructions that point at each picture ('put @Image1 into @Image2')
Also writes a picture from words alone
limits: Standard size only: no large or print-size output
Wide, tall or square frames only
Previous generation; Kling 3.0 image looks better but takes one reference picture here
Words in the picture aren't reliable
kling-o1.best_for: Combining a person, product and setting from separate pictures
kling-o1.tip: Call pictures @Image1, @Image2 in the order attached, and say how they relate: 'Place the woman from @Image1 in the kitchen from @Image2.'

ltx-2-fast.summary: The quick tier of LTX-2, Lightricks' late-2025 generation. Writes a clip from words or animates a still, with sound. Replaced by LTX 2.5 Fast.
good: Quick, and makes sound with the picture
Large frame sizes for a fast model
Animates a start frame as well as writing from words
Costs less than LTX 2.5 Fast
limits: No frame-shape setting, so you can't ask for vertical or square
Clips are 6, 8 or 10 seconds only
No end frame and no seed
Older generation; LTX 2.5 Fast is the newer version

p-video-animate.summary: Pruna's motion transfer. The character in your still copies the movement, camera move and sound of a driving clip, so you can record one performance and reuse it on many characters.
good: Copies a real performance onto a still: a dance, a gesture, talking
Keeps the still's look, wardrobe and background
Works on illustrated characters and mascots as well as photos
Keeps the driving clip's sound
limits: Needs both a still and a driving clip
Fast action, cuts, and things passing in front of the subject make it less consistent
No prompt in the Studio: you steer it only with the clip and the still
p-video-animate.best_for: Making a mascot or character perform a recorded move

sd1.5-epicrealism.summary: epiCRealism, a popular Stable Diffusion 1.5 photo-realism model by the community creator epinikion. Cheap, fast and dated.
good: Natural, unpolished photo look for portraits and simple scenes
Very cheap and fast
Takes an 'avoid' list and a seed
limits: SD 1.5 generation: weak hands and anatomy, no readable text
Small, square pictures in the Studio
Loses track of prompts with several subjects

sam-v2-image.summary: Meta's Segment Anything 2 for stills (2024). Outlines an object you name or point to and returns a mask. Replaced by SAM 3.
good: Fast, almost free masks from a word or a point.
Clean outlines on well-defined objects.
Takes points on the picture as well as words, so you can pick exactly which object.
limits: Older generation: SAM 3 understands far more kinds of thing from words.
Returns a mask or overlay, not a finished picture.
sam-v2-image.best_for: A quick mask of one object

sdxl1.0-nightvis-lightning.summary: NightVision XL in a fast version: a community SDXL photo-realism model. One of several fast realism models here; choose between them by look.
good: Photo-style pictures in a few seconds
Cheap
Takes an 'avoid' list and a seed
limits: Older SDXL generation: hands, text and complex prompts trail today's models
Square pictures only

seedance-1.0-pro-fast.summary: A fast, very cheap version of Seedance 1.0 Pro. It makes silent clips from words or a start frame. Handy for rough motion tests and animatics where cost matters more than polish.
good: One of the cheapest video options in the Studio, and quick.
Decent motion and camera following for rough drafts and animatics.
Can start from a still, so Board keyframes can be animated cheaply for a first look.
limits: No sound.

No end frame and no reference pictures.

seedance-1.0-pro-fast.best_for: Cheap rough animatics from Board keyframes

seedream-5-pro-layer-decomposition.summary: Not a generator. It takes one finished picture and splits it into cut-out layers, each object on its own see-through layer, plus a clean background with the hidden parts filled in. For designers who need to move or swap pieces.
good: Pulls each main object onto its own transparent layer, ready for Photoshop, Figma or Canva.
Fills in the background behind whatever it lifts out, so the backdrop stands on its own.

Works best on clear, well-separated objects. Cluttered or overlapping scenes split less cleanly.
It only separates. It doesn't create anything new or change the picture.
seedream-5-pro-layer-decomposition.best_for: Turning a flat poster or product shot into editable layers
seedream-5-pro-layer-decomposition.tip: List the pieces you want, each with a colour or position: 'the orange mug, the green plant on the left, the stack of books'. You get cleaner cut-outs and a predictable bill.

gemini-omni-1.1-video-edit.summary: The Change mode of Google's Gemini Omni 1.1. Upload a short clip, describe one change, and it applies it while keeping everything else: restyle, swap or recolour a product, add or remove objects.

Background swaps relight the subject to match.
A cheap draft size for testing ideas.

Long, detailed instructions cause edits you didn't ask for.

sdxl1.0-dyanvis-lightning.summary: DynaVision XL in a fast version: a community SDXL model for stylised 3D animated-film looks, in the spirit of Pixar and DreamWorks.

Fast and cheap
Good for playful, family-friendly concepts

Square pictures only

flux-realism-lora.summary: FLUX.1 Dev with XLabs AI's Realism LoRA (a small add-on trained to push a photographic look), plus an optional upscale step. An early community attempt to make FLUX look less like AI.

Cheap.
Wide choice of shapes.

higgsfield-soul-2.summary: Higgsfield's Soul 2.0: fashion-editorial photoreal pictures with taste built in. It understands fashion terms, camera language and internet aesthetics; one optional reference picture sets the vibe.

Tuned for fashion and people; not the pick for diagrams, packaging or text-led work.

ideogram-v4-fast.summary: Ideogram 4.0 (June 2026) on Ideogram's own service, with a speed-versus-quality setting. Cheap, large, text-led design pictures.

One of the cheapest text specialists here, with large files.
Good for posters, thumbnails, flyers and packaging mock-ups.
limits: Portraits and photoreal faces are its weakest area.
No seed and no reference pictures.
Older than Ideogram 4.5.

wan-alpha.summary: A words-to-video model whose clips come on a transparent background (a real see-through layer), ready to lay over other footage. Built on Alibaba's open Wan 2.1 video model.

Handles smoke, glass, glow and fine hair, which green-screen keying struggles with.
Cheap for a video model.

Delivers WebM with transparency, which some players and editors don't show correctly.
wan-alpha.best_for: Overlay elements: smoke, sparks, a lone subject to layer over footage
wan-alpha.tip: Always include 'transparent background' and a shot type (close-up, medium shot, wide shot) in the prompt, or the subject may land on a solid background.

bria-extract-object.summary: Bria's tool for pulling one named object out of a picture as a transparent cutout: one product from a flat-lay, one person from a group. Trained on licensed images.

Soft, natural edges, ready to drop into a new background
Can lift a subject made of several parts
Licensed-data training
limits: One object per run
When there are similar objects you must say which one ('the mug on the right')
