makers.Alibaba: One of China's largest e-commerce and cloud companies, and one of the busiest AI makers in the Studio. Its Tongyi Lab makes the Wan video and image models (early ones released openly, known for strong motion and camera control; Wan 3.0 adds long takes with sound) and the small, fast Z-Image. The Qwen team's image models are known above all for readable text in pictures, and HappyHorse, from its Taotian shopping group, makes video with matching speech.
makers.Black Forest Labs: A German lab started by former Stability AI researchers; FLUX is their family. The tier words repeat across generations: Schnell and Klein are the small fast ones, Dev the open version, Pro the standard paid model, Flex adds tuning dials, Max is the top tier and Kontext the instruction editor. FLUX 3 (2026) is their first model that makes video with sound as well as stills.
makers.Bria: Bria is an Israeli company that trains its image models only on licensed pictures from more than 30 partners, Getty Images among them, and pays the owners through an attribution system. That is its main selling point for commercial work. Its range is practical: cutouts, new backgrounds, expanding, upscaling, plus the FIBO models for making and editing pictures.
makers.ByteDance: TikTok's parent company. Its Seed team makes the Seedream still-image models, known for clean text in pictures and precise edits, and the Seedance video models, known for sound made with the picture, several shots in one clip and large reference kits. Pro is the top tier; Lite, Fast and Mini are cheaper, quicker versions that give up some quality, and Seedance refuses photos of real people's faces.
makers.Clarity AI: Clarity AI began as an open-source upscaler billed as a free alternative to Magnific and grew into a paid service. Most of its upscalers are creative and invent new detail; Crystal is its faithful one.
makers.Community: Independent creators who take an open model like SD 1.5 or SDXL and train or blend it toward one look: realistic people, anime, 3D cartoons, fantasy art. Most share their work on Civitai, a model-sharing site, and Segmind hosts some of the popular ones. Each tends to have one narrow strength rather than all-round skill, and all share their base model's weak spots.
makers.ControlNet (Lvmin Zhang): ControlNet is an add-on, published in 2023 by the Stanford researcher Lvmin Zhang, that makes an image model follow a guide picture: its outlines, its depth, a scribble or a body pose. It made 'you set the layout, the AI paints it' practical, and versions now exist for most open models. The ones here are the original SD 1.5 set.
makers.ESRGAN (Xintao Wang): ESRGAN and its successor Real-ESRGAN came from academic and Tencent ARC research led by Xintao Wang. They became the classic free upscalers: faithful and fast, but an older generation.
makers.fal: A US company that hosts AI models and tunes some of its own. With MiniMax it built H3 Max, a quicker, lower-resolution version of H3, and H3 Max Turbo, which is quicker and cheaper still.
makers.fofr: fofr is a well-known builder on Replicate who makes open workflows by chaining SDXL-era tools such as InstantID and ControlNet. The results are fun and cheap, but they date from before today's reference-picture models.
makers.Google: Google's AI lab. It makes the Nano Banana image models (Gemini's image side), strong on text, layout and blending many reference pictures, and the Veo and Gemini Omni video models, which make sound with the picture. Its video models refuse real people's likenesses.
makers.HeyGen: An AI avatar company best known for talking-presenter videos. Its models train on photos of one person and keep that face consistent across looks and videos.
makers.HiDream: A Chinese start-up whose open-source HiDream-I1 image model (MIT licence, 2025) is known for good prompt following among open models. The fast version trades detail for speed and price.
makers.Higgsfield: A creator-focused AI photo and video company. Its Soul image models aim for pictures that look photographed rather than rendered, with strong fashion and style sense; its DoP video model animates stills with preset camera effects.
makers.Ideogram: A Toronto-based lab whose models are known above all for spelling words correctly inside pictures. Each generation is aimed at design work (posters, logos, packaging, signs) rather than photorealism, and portraits are a known weak spot. Ideogram 4.0 (2026) was its first open-weight model; 4.5 is the newest.
makers.InstantX: An open-source research team known for InstantID (keeping a face from one photo) and for early guide add-ons (ControlNets) for SD 3 and FLUX. Their SD 3 Medium add-ons here follow outlines, a body pose, or the picture's own colours and layout.
makers.Kling: Kling is the video and image line from Kuaishou, the Chinese short-video company, first released in 2024 and known for natural human motion and believable physics. Version numbers (1.6, 2.1, 2.6, 3.0) are generations; Standard and Pro are a lighter draft tier and a higher-quality tier of the same model. The 'O' (Omni) line, O1 then O3, is built to work from reference pictures and to edit existing footage, not just make clips from words.
makers.Kolors (Kuaishou): Kolors is an open image model from a separate team at Kuaishou, released in 2024 and unrelated to the Kling video line. It is quick and cheap, and its main distinction was handling Chinese prompts and Chinese text.
makers.Krea: A creative-tools company that co-trained FLUX.1 Krea with Black Forest Labs. Its aim was a more natural, less over-polished photographic look than stock FLUX.
makers.Lightricks: Lightricks, the Israeli company behind Facetune and LTX Studio, makes the LTX video models. They are fast and cheap, several are released as open models anyone can run, and from LTX-2 onward they make sound with the picture. LTX 2.5 comes in a Fast tier that goes bigger and longer and a Pro tier tuned for quality.
makers.Lodestone Rock: Lodestone Rock is the independent developer behind Chroma, a community-funded open model retrained from FLUX.1 schnell. It is known for being open and lightly filtered.
makers.Luma: A US video-AI company. Its Ray models are known for smooth, cinematic camera moves; Modify Video restyles real footage while keeping the performance; Uni-1 is a newer image model that reasons through an instruction before drawing.
makers.Meta: Facebook's parent company. Its Segment Anything (SAM) models don't make pictures: they find and outline objects in stills and video, which is useful for masks and cut-outs.
makers.MiniMax: A Shanghai AI company whose video models are sold as Hailuo and, since mid-2026, as the H series (H3 is also called Hailuo 3). Hailuo models are known for natural body motion and facial acting, and H3 adds much sharper output and longer takes. 'Fast' versions are cheaper, quicker cuts of the same model.
makers.Monster Labs: Monster Labs is a community group that released the QR Code Monster ControlNet, the tool behind hidden-pattern and scannable-QR artwork.
makers.OminiControl (NUS): OminiControl is a research project from the National University of Singapore that adds picture control (like keeping a given object) to FLUX models with a very small add-on.
makers.OpenAI: The company behind ChatGPT. Its GPT Image models follow instructions closely, write legible text in pictures and make careful edits that leave the rest of a picture alone. Its Sora video models are being retired: OpenAI scheduled the Sora video API to shut down in September 2026.
makers.Philip Hofmann: Philip Hofmann is a community trainer of open upscaling models, including the Nomos8k photo models. His models aim for natural-looking, faithful enlargements.
makers.PixVerse: PixVerse comes from AISphere, a Beijing start-up. Its models are quick and inexpensive, aimed at social content, with a polished, slightly stylized look. V6 (2026) added sound, longer clips, Extend and a reference mode; the V5, 4.5 and unnumbered entries are older generations.
makers.Pruna: Pruna AI is a European start-up whose speciality is making AI models run faster and cheaper. Its P Image and P Video lines are built for speed and low cost, some on its own models and some on other companies' (Ideogram, MiniMax's H3, Lightricks' LTX-2). Expect quick, inexpensive results that sit below the flagship models in polish.
makers.Qwen Edit add-ons: Developers, many of them independent, train small add-ons (LoRAs: extra training on example pictures that teaches one skill) on top of Alibaba's open Qwen Image Edit 2509. Each does one job, such as relighting, erasing or changing the camera angle. They are cheap and quick, but their quality is capped by the 2025 editor underneath.
makers.Recraft: A design-tool company whose models are built for graphic designers rather than photo realism. It is the main source of AI models that output true editable vector (SVG) files, and its V4 line (2026) is pitched on 'design taste': tidy layouts, cohesive colour and legible type.
makers.RunDiffusion: The team behind Juggernaut, one of the most popular community retunes of open image models, later rebuilt on FLUX. Juggernaut models chase natural skin and sharper photo detail over the stock look.
makers.Runway: A New York company and one of the first AI video tools for filmmakers. Its Gen models animate a start frame quickly and dependably, without sound, and Aleph edits existing footage: restyle it, add or remove things, find new angles.
makers.S-Lab (NTU): S-Lab at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore is a research lab whose CodeFormer became a standard tool for restoring faces. Its licence limits commercial use.
makers.Sber: Russia's largest bank, whose AI arm makes the open Kandinsky image and video models. Kandinsky 6.0 includes a video upscaler that sharpens short clips without flicker.
makers.Segmind: Segmind is the service the Studio uses to reach every model. It also makes a few small, fast models of its own (SSD-1B, Vega) and hosts many open community models and ready-made workflows under its name, most of them from the SDXL era.
makers.Stability AI: The London company behind the open SD image models (SD 1.5, SDXL, SD 3 and SD 3.5) that started the open AI-picture boom in 2022. Because the models were free to adapt, thousands of community versions and add-ons were built on them, and many models in this list are exactly that. They're cheap and flexible, but trail today's flagships on hands, text in pictures and following long prompts.
makers.Tencent: The Chinese tech giant behind WeChat. Its WeChat AI team built Wan Alpha on Alibaba's open Wan 2.1 video model so that clips come out on a transparent background.
makers.Topaz Labs: Topaz Labs is a US company long known for desktop photo and video enhancement software (Gigapixel, Topaz Video AI) that photographers and editors rely on. Its upscalers aim to stay faithful: bigger, sharper and cleaner, without redrawing the picture.
makers.VEED: A London-based online video editor. Its background-removal model cuts people and objects out of footage without a green screen.
makers.xAI: Elon Musk's AI company, maker of Grok. Its Grok Imagine models are quick and fairly permissive: the images are strong on text and layout, and the clips come with sound, though reviewers rate their motion and physics below the very best.
makers.XLabs AI: A small team that released some of the first community add-ons for FLUX.1 Dev in 2024, such as a realism LoRA and an IP-Adapter for borrowing a picture's look. Useful in their day, but they sit on a 2024 base and newer models do the same jobs better.
makers.XPixel Group: XPixel is an academic research group focused on image restoration and upscaling. Its SUPIR model rebuilds badly damaged photos by generating new detail.
makers.Zhipu AI: A Chinese AI company spun out of Tsinghua University. Its CogVideoX models were among the first capable open video models in 2024 and are now well behind current ones.
